This game is a lot of fun and despite some of the more stressful aspects of the game it's a pretty great shift if you're looking for something to relax to while playing. The controls are mostly intuitive and those that aren't are well taught (for some reason I can't make myself naturally reverse the right and left click for their functionality because I am used to games like 7 Days to Die where the place button is a right-click...). The scenery is beautiful and the diet to slime husbandry affectation is a pretty wonderful use of mechanics. On the whole I have to say that the game is a wonderful experience and I am enjoying myself a lot. My two rebukes are these: (1) First, I understand that this is a loosely scripted game wherein you play a certain character and the events, communications, and interactions are controlled. I am not a huge fan of this in the multiplayer era. I am not saying that this should be shunted to the side, but perhaps a range of characters available with slightly different areas and challenges where a small group of friends might be able to trade slimes indigenous to their starting regions, challenge one another, or maybe even have weird little contests like eating contests, or biggest slime at a "fair", perhaps there could be a chance for the player(s) to meet each other and the NPCs during these events. I am just saying that some multiplayer could work. (2) The world is just too small with too little to do. In my fourth hour I was rather bored as I had the best slimes I could at that point in the game, explored everything, and had everything on automatic handling. Too put it simply there needs to be more. I know that by the looks of things the devs are working on it, but the game is just extremely short at the moment with very little content. I worry that over time this will become another Stranded Deep with an impressive game with endless potential having no content for so long that it becomes a thing of the past. I don't want that for Slime Rancher, I want it to succeed and developed little squishball wrist rest gel relaxer cushion hybrid slime toys that are strangely weird to touch but endlessly satisfying anyways, I want to see people showing up with vac-packs and cowboy/girl get-ups at conventions, I want people to make their very own plorts and veggies/fruits from the game to have around as cool toys or maybe even candy! So go forth DEVs, and be FRUITful!!!

Day 33 of gameplay and something unspeakable happens.
By this point I had mastered the game. Over 60,000$, fully upgraded everything. I could pump out 200+ plorts in a day no problem. The stock market had crashed with how much I sold and it had gotten to the point where I had three silos filled to the brim with plorts and I didn't have enough patience to sell them. Eventually churning out plorts gets boring. So I released most of my slimes, and now I keep four slimes in each cage, name them, keep them well fed with their favourite foods. I even feed the local slimes outside my home if I have time.
One day I was going about business when I saw a pink slime had wandered into my farm (I don't keep pink slimes, I find them annoying) Now, ten days prior I would have fired him straight into the sea to see the rest of his murdered family, but he was so bouncy and I was a somewhat of a Slime Activist now, so let him live.
Days past. Weeks. I get attached to the slime, naming him Wanderer. I feed him a balenced diet of chickens, fruits and veggies. I swear he loved me! Sometimes he jumped on my head and he would follow me around as I fed the other slimes.
Day 33 dawns like any other day. I get up and do my daily duties. Wanderer is hopping around and I throw some carrots at him for breakfast. I leave after my chores to get some fresh water for the puddle slimes and I come back with some pogo fruits for him. As I round the corner I see him hopping towards me. But, unbeknownst to him the Exchange machine was online and asking for pink slimes. I see his smiling face coming towards me, and I readied my gun to shoot the pogo fruit for him to catch when  *poof* he's gone. Wanderer vanished. I look at the Exchange machine's screen and it says, "1/12 Pink Slimes"
He had ♥♥♥♥ing sacrificed himself to the Exchange machine in his doglike haste to greet me.
I was frozen in shock for a good three minutes before I quit the game. I haven't been on it since.
RIP Wanderer. Day 14?-33

The best word to sum up SteamWorld Dig is "transparent".
The game loop consists entirely of going into the mine, collecting ore, going back up, selling it, buying +1 to your pick, and repeating. It is an extremely mindless and unchallenging way to spend 3 hours. It's not fun or interesting at any point.
I get it. All games require some sort of loop to keep you playing it and keeping the feel consistent. But SteamWorld is, as I said, completely transparent. Nothing exciting or shocking happens, there are no interesting puzzles to solve, challenging monsters to battle, or interesting characters to talk to. There's nowhere to explore, and nowhere to go but deeper into the mine, where the gems are a new color and the numbers are bigger.
If, like me, you play this game to the end, you will hate it and yourself all the way through for being so obviously manipulated into dull, glassy-eyed complacency by a skinner box's "reward" of a bigger number next to your mining pick. Do yourself a favor and don't buy it - and if you have bought it, just say no. Life's too short for this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t.

TL;DR
Best fighting game imo, badass characters, cute waifus, great soundtracks, go click that "Add to cart" button already
OPINION
I gotta be honest, this game is what makes me love fighting games, got me hooked for 10 hours straight for testing all characters, watching the story, fishing (yeah, you can get figurines, music, and collectibles), etc. I prefer keyboard over usual controllers because there are 6 buttons (actually 5, 1 is a macro)
STORY
The story is pretty confusing if you are new to the series, which is why GG put a terminology button if the players are confused with the words.
GAMEPLAY
Guilty Gear is a fast-paced fighting game with lots of characters with different playstyle.
For example:
Sol Badguy: an all-rounder which makes it perfect for newcomers
Sin Kiske: a character who deals huge damage and easy to execute combos, but requires appetite gauge. If a player tries to make Sin do a special move with zero appetite gauge, he will be "stunned" and will be more vulnerable to attacks
Jack-O: Summons her minions, and can explode them on command, dealing huge damage
Potemkin: a slow character who can't run, but has huge defense and great throwing power, keep your distance if you are fighting him.
Chipp: he can teleport to either enemy's front, back, or above, a very fast character with unpredictable moves, but has the lowest defense of the game
After all that, there are some mechanics that makes GG unique to other fighting games:
Tension gauge: filled by moving to your opponent, dealing and receiving damage, tension gauge can be used for Roman Cancels, Overdrives, and much more.
Roman Cancel: slows down time for a while and cancels your action, making it perfect to execute more combos or escape from enemy projectiles. Uses 25% tension gauge
I can go on for a more lengthy review but I'm too lazy to type all of it. There's so many to love from this game, I really recommend this game to everyone who loves fighting games.

DICETINY: The Lord of the Dice is a board/card game with RPG elements. This game is in Early Access, and at the moment it does not have too much content.

When I first started playing this, first thought what come to my mind that its a bit looks like Hearthstone, but this not that.
This basically a board game with cards. In every turn you and your opponent roll a dice and move around a board, the two characters moving in different way, one start a circle from left, other from right. The game will be end when someone has no more HP. If you arrive for a land with enemy, you fight , but if that enemy is neutral you have a option to hire it.

You can use a different cards, some cards boost you, some put down friendly minions, etc. If you want play a card, this cost some points what you get in every turn. At the start you have one character to play, other you can unlock when you beat them in the story mode. All heroes have own special abilities and cards as well. Also you can create your own card decks.

The graphic style is a caricatured carton, and this looks nice. Sounds and music also good.

So my verdict

+complected with humor
+nice graphics
+steam cards
+cheaper in EA than later when got full version
+fast matches

-at the moment not too much content
-no multiplayer
-no steam achievements

The gameplay is your standard ORION game, defend [Blank], kill [Blank], and stay alive while helping your team. The big difference with this game from the others is the 3 gameplay cameras that can be swapped with the F1 key. You have your top-down view similar to Halo Spartan Assualt, The Mass Effect 3rd person camera, and your usual first person camera. The guns handle well and there seems to be some sort of crafting system. You have two PvE game modes, with PvP game modes coming soon.
You still have your cosmetics and the such with 2 forms of in game currency. These can be earned while playing or puchased.
TL;DR: Really good game for $1. I recommend it, and it's really fun to play with friends.

SMB is a great game with a couple problems that will no doubt infuriate some people. To start, using a DS4 controller with Input Mapper I must immediately put deadzones down to -50. Yes, a negative deadzone, otherwise the game to me is almost unplayable with a gaping hole of a deadzone that is impossible to get past for me. I cannot remember if the PS4 version has this deadzone, but I will have to check that out.
Getting beyond that, there is actually a lot of content here. Dark worlds, extra characters with new controls, and a hefty normal campaign that gets pretty difficult. The controls when you tune deadzone are pretty good, but some traditionalists may never get the hang of them. Physics can be really weird at times, and your hands are going to get a big workout just from trying to precisey maneuver Meatboy around.
The art style is pretty cool, and the cinematics are funny. I love the over the top gore in this game, and it gives the hilarious characters a nice depth of personality. Seeing Meatboy beat up time and time again in his search for the girl never gets old. But I don't think the graphics are going to blow your mind. In short, it's a decent indie experience.
I play the game is small increments, otherwise I notice a tendency to dislike the game and its trial and error approach. If you take it slow I think the game is very rewarding. Even watching a couple guides might help you not lose so much time to trial and error. All in all I recommend this one to platformer fans. Not sure about anyone else that is averse to difficulty both due to game design and unfortunate controller problems.

Steamworld Dig is a very addictive experience that unfortunately falls somewhat short of being a great game. I have rarely been so conflicted while writing a review. On one hand, the great aesthetics, entertaining exploration and gratifying upgrades kept me coming back for more. On the other, the game rarely presents much of a challenge, rarely testing your/Rusty's abilities.
The graphics are charming, the environments and NPCs memorable, and the sense of exploration is great...and then you realize it's all over with little sense of real accomplishment (well, as much accomplishment as one can glean from playing a video-game).
It's definitely a short and sweet experience, and you will likely find yourself addicted for the 5-9 hours or so it will take to complete the game, but unfortunately the limited depth and replayability means few will be coming back to this one. I would love to see this world fleshed out in a more in-depth sequel with more to explore, more/more intelligent enemies, and more combat abilities/general abilities in your arsenal.

DiceTiny sells itself as a dice and card based board game, augmented with abilities and gold. This sounds great and I was really excited however the game is extremely unbalanced, and almost random. My first game I tried playing minions which for the most part just got killed by my opponent with no effect to him, often 2-3 at a time. Which was followed shortly after with me pretty much 1 hitting him for a large chunk of his health. There is also a lot of small problems, for example the opponents turn moves so fast you often can’t read your opponents cards, so you have no idea what’s going on and how your opponent just killed all your stuff with 1 card. There is no description of what abilities do, I had a card with absorb, but have no clue what it does. The Game is Early access so I can excuse the extremely limited Deckbuilding and lack of other features, but just note this if you choose to buy. I have also heard of crash issues but didn’t have any myself. I could mention a lot of other small things, but ultimately the game isn’t really worth your money at this point I might keep an eye on the patch notes for improvements.

I joined Steam recently and this was one of the first games I purchased. I have since completed the game and I love the depicted Victorian era and British English.
Growing up reading Sherlock Holmes novels, his methods of deduction remains elusive to me. This game guides you to solving the mystery from a first-person perspective of Sherlock Holmes or Dr. Watson.
I have read reviews lamenting that the game play leans more towards running errands for NPCs. But I think it introduces the player to the NPCs. And running errands build up trust between them, hence the inclination to provide information that they otherwise would not tell the police.
In particular, the story is congruous with the alleged crimes by Jack the Ripper in Whitechapel. The ending is great and characteristic of Sherlock Holmes' eccentricity. All in all, the story unfolded at a pace that kept me tether to the screen. Good job, Frogwares!

This is one of the experiences that will stick with you. Adventure games, games as a whole, even the movie industry(from the surprise ending) has something to learn from this game.

Do you like classic Victorian era Sherlock Holmes?
Are you intrigued by the Whitechapel murders of 1888?
Then you will love this game!
Cleverly the game developers have meshed together these two iconic characters into one very plausible story. You play as Detective Sherlock Holmes and his companion Dr John Watson either in first or third person perspective (depending on taste) as you investigate the five canonical victims of Jack the Ripper.
While this game suffers from PS2/Xbox era graphics (It looked dated even at its time of release) it does however still manage to conjure up a very detailed, authentic, and atmospheric London of the period.
Puzzles can be frustrating at times especially those that do not directly impact the murder cases themselves but overlook this fault and there is plenty to enjoy here.
I would recommend this game and I give it a solid 8/10

This Sherlock Holmes adventure game is a step above the previous entry from these Developers, "The Awakened" but ultimately it is still frustrating, awkward, and unfun.
I love adventure games and Sherlock Holmes, so I was feeling pretty motivated to slog my way through the slow or frustrating parts, but in the end the problems with the game defeated me.
Firstly, I had the same problem that I experienced with The Awakened, in that every time to load up the game, I freeze at a black screen for about 5 minutes, though the game plays well after that. I tried all the suggested fixes from the forum, including copying PhysX DLL files to the game's directory, but I was never able to solve this issue.
The gameplay itself is alright, but you will find yourself mostly doing petty fetch quests, and solving poorly-explained, awkwardly designed puzzles. There's also the issue that often crops up when games are developed by non-English speakers, as some of the writing is just odd, sounds off, or in some cases just plain don't make sense.
Lastly, you can switch between first and third person to navigate the world, which is good, since something about these Frogrwares games gives me immediate nausea in the first-person persepective.
I wanted to like this game, I tried to like it, but in the end I had to admit I don't like it very much at all.

The MP can get a little quirky for the host, but it should be resolved in the next update according to the DEVS most recent streams. I highly recommend the game, if you do want to wait for a sale that's up to you but it's worth the price tag and the hours you probably felt just flew by.

Better than modern XCOM games.
Lovingly awaiting the sequel, and hopefully eventual Terror From the Deep remake.
Only thing letting it down is lack of final polish - Quicksave works, Quickload doesn't, for example. It's still a solid game both in the turn based genre and in the XCOM genre, for sure. Could use a little more "XCOMMY" type features, like having to capture medics, navigators, and leader versions of enemies, having access to psionics, and armour that features directional based damage rather than just invisible extra hitpoints, but it's great regardless. There's a fair bit of unfinished content still lurking in the game files, but most has been restored by mods so that's a moot point.
One thing that stands out is the severe attention to detail this game was given. Both the sci-fi fluff of the research trees and all the technology you discover, research and unlock have fantastic amounts of detail that is both believable and a joy to read - complete with pictures and written from a "human" perspective so it feels less like a wikipedia article and more like someones report, too.
The other would be the attention to detail the maps have, since the game features Z-Levels, as you go up and down them, certain large objects and buildings get sliced apart so you can see into the inner workings - one such example being the turrets in the Xenonaut base - it's all very detailed and you can see the sheer amount of work the artist/s put into it all. Rare to come across a game these days that someone has put so much love and care into. Much credit is due for that.
With an active modding community with plenty of mods that extend and increase various facets of the game as a whole, not to mention an incredibly easy to tweak bunch of main game files in the form of .xml documents so you can change various parts of the game to fit more to your playstyle (for example, if a funding country leaves the Xenonaut Project, you can "free" them again by destroying a base in said region - this is off by default, but can be turned on through the .xml files) this game definitely has plenty of life in it and will earn a place in your library. There's even a "Community Edition" mod you can acquire that comes preloaded with a huge suite of lore friendly, vanillaesque mods that will expand and improve the base game from the get go, such as Lore+ which adds even more detailed and rich research topics.
Like turn based games? Like the XCOM genre? Buy it, play it, you'll enjoy it. It's worth your money and your time.

Pitting England's most prolific fictional detective against it's most notorious real life serial killer seems an obvious fit and even more surprising when both Holmesian lore and the actual murder case are done justice. Investigating the crime scenes, gathering clues and discovering the how's and why's of the whodunit are genuinely intriguing, at times even unbearably creepy. When not on your investigation it's a hokey puzzle game full of fetch quests and vague, rigid solutions that at best hold your hand until you answer it correctly. The blame and praise lay solely on it's halfhearted developer Frogwares for not pushing the material past puzzle game fare into adventure territory. Add to this a nonsensical ending and the game's limitations are impossible to overlook. There's this rich Victorian environment to explore, an evocative dichotomy of good and evil in Holmes and The Ripper, but while true to the material and often engaging there's no real cat & mouse in the chase.

I applaud them for having the price cheaper while in early access than it will be once it's released out of early access.  Usually it's the other way around.
That said, the game is definitely an early access game.  Content is limited.  But what there is, is good, and in my opinion it's worth investing in this game in the hope for more content.
Graphics style is gritty cartoon and caricature.  Oversized heads, bulging muscles, punches to the face, etc.  There's a lot of humor in this game and pop culture references.
It's basically a board game with cards.  You and an opponent take turns rolling dice and moving around a board.  When you land on a space there might be a neutral enemy you can either fight to get gold or hire them so that they will fight the opponent.  The battles are just one hit and then they are done, it does not continue until someone dies.  So basically you're trying to whittle down your opponents HP to zero over time.   Each game I've played has been fairly short, so it's not like a long drawn out campaign.
You can use cards to lay down friendly minions, spells to harm enemies, movement spells to move you where you want to go, and other options.   But those cost action points to use and you only have so many action points per turn.
There are different characters you can play and they each have their own special abilites and cards.  That makes for a nice variety in playstyle.
tl;dr breakdown:
Card game on a square board. (or a board game with cards!)
Early Access
Limited content at this time with promise of more coming
Play as different characters, each with own style and cards
Short games - good for a quick gaming fix
Humor (the title scroll is hilarous)

Dicetiny is a fun little dice rolling and deck building game. In the video above we show a short preview of a game on the beginning level.
Fakedice provided a review copy of Dicetiny to The Hidden Levels and for that we thank them greatly.
My first impression was that the UI was very similar to a certain card game I play on occasion. The artwork is very similar in the deckbuilder only however, so we can move past that. The cards are interesitng and the rest of the artwork is highly stylized in a good looking package of minions, creatures, characters, and cards.
The game mechanics are also interesting albeit not groundbreaking in terms of a board game. You roll dice to move around the board, playing cards and defeating minions until one of the two players is at zero health. The unique aspect seems to be the character abilities such as giving a minion +1 damage, or giving your character +2 attack power. That's it essentially, you roll dice and play cards, attempting to defeat your opponenet or minions. You can alternatively pay to hire some minions which became fun when our hero was able to give them more attack power with his special ability.
The replay value is relatively high, you can gain more cards and heros, build decks, and play consistently without it being a repetitive experience. The game is stilll in early access so the potential for more additions is more than a certainty. There are also a substantial number of gaming related "easter eggs" or small jokes relating to other games. It took me a bit to realize that "Middle Board" was a play on Lord of the rings. There is a solid mix of humor, strategy, and fun that seems to make this a solid board game experience for the PC.
I'd recommend picking this one up if you have any plans to play it, especially since during Early Acess it appears to be substantially discounted. The price increase will be corrolating to the addition of more content towards release and it appears that it will leave Early Access at the $20 price point. I plan on coming back to it each time they unlock more levels and content.

Likes:

Dislikes:

Once you get everything, there even isn't a point to go to any more worlds unless if you just wan't to explore.
It's horrible to travel though, waiting for the planets to orbit with no option to fly to planet directly even for more fuel cost to you, is just a horrible design for impatient people.
Co-op just wasn't working well for my friends. They got disconnected a lot. When they did they lost all their stuff in inventory. It would fall to the ground. Even their weapon fell to the ground. We couldn't remove their weapon off the ground even though they got a new one. Basically it would stay on your world glitched for life. People joining you would lag horribly. Just wasn't too smooth of a co-op.
Falling through the world? I thought that was a thing for people with bad ISPs and scrap metal pc's from caveman gaming parts and caveman isp's. That needs fixed.

You will have to lower volume in windows or lose hearing without the option to sue the game devs for damages done to you over time so lower sounds in windows to not lose hearing. No way for the game to save these options for you as it is currently broken. Been that way since launch and no fix to it. Something that basic can't be fixed in months. That's just sad. Probably means it's also that their team is just one person or not enough dedicated people in the team to do that type of stuff. Talking to people is rough since they have to raise their mic volumes in chat programs you use just so you can hear them enough since your sounds are low due to poor volume design from the game dev(s).

: Bill tells me you played Dark Souls once.
: Yeah.
: [examining Dark Souls 2] How does this one compare to that one?
: If you're gonna compare a Dark Souls game, you compare it to every other game ever made... that wasn't Dark Souls .
The Good:
+Jolly cooperation now works like magic, goodbye GFWL
+Better PC port, smooth FPS right out of the box, no mod needed
+You can now dual wield anything
+Talking cute cat
+Guard break: solves the problem of greatshield VS greatshield situation
The meh..:
-Boring bosses. Still kick your♥♥♥♥♥though, but nothing you'll remember like the Four Kings or Knight Artorias or The Gaping Dragon or any other bosses from previous Souls series.
-Lighting effect does not work well in this game. You'll need graphic mod installed to fully immerse yourself in the kingdom of Drangelic. The torch still functions and will save your day in some situations, but it was rather limited.
-You can't send a hate mail via steam. I miss GFWL for this sole reason.
The bad:
-Poise mechanic is a bit weird, and nobody knows why a single punch from ceastus will instantly stunlock you.
The real game will start in NG+. Or so I've heard. Yes, Dark Souls 2 feels a bit too easy - particularly because Fromsoft has been generous in distributing bonfires in this game, some bonfire was situated just before the boss area fog gate (and coop worked way too excellent, a good caster in your party will have the boss defeated in no time).
However, if you're in mood for the real hardmode, you can always enter the Covenant of Champions which will totally disable coop with other players and you can't summon NPCs as well.
As for which one is better, I'd say Dark Souls 1 is a lot better. Story and lore in Dark Souls 2 lacking, there is just nothing to care about the NPC. No memorable character like Solaire of Astora. Benhart of Jugo is cheerful enough but you just like him because his Moonlight Greatsword.
Prepare for Jolly Cooperation!

This is still VERY early access. I'd go so far as to call it an open alpha. The game lags consistantly and that's the best that it runs. I'm playing on a fairly new Macbook so it's not hardware and I haven't ruled out formatting issues.
As far as actual gameplay goes Dicetiny unapologetically rips from Hearthstone, even down to their card designs and abilities. Though I am looking foreward to a collectable card game that is not pay-to-win. I already play Mtg and I don't need to spend the rest of my income on virtual cards...
The other major source of insperation for gameplay is Monopoly, thats where the board game part of the formula comes in. If you've ever played monopoly just imagine Dicetiny as a hybrid of that and Hearthstone and thats all thats about all thats going on here aside from the... "humor", but I'll get back to that. Calling those two games "influences" is like saying CoD:MW really only laid the ground work for the innovations CoD:MW2,3,6,&11 brought to the table. I feel like theres so much room to do intresting things with this format. Maybe take a few more liberties with card design, or if the creators are only intrested in mashing up existing ip's why not try Mario Party? A board with multiple routes would offer tons of gamplay variation. Or perhaps multiplayer?
And then theres the humor... This game had me really excited to see the writing. I thought the tag lines about "popculture" couldn't be sincere and that Dicetiny was mascerading as a shallow experence, but would develop into some kind of subversion of tropes and expectations, and perhaps commenting on the very nature of "pop culture" itself. Damn was I wrong. Watch the trailers and you get a pretty good idea of what your in for. Without spoiling anything(at this point there really isnt much to spoil) the opening starts with a long crawl of text(yes like star wars) that has a lot of words which provided a sentence's worth of story and an obscene amount of jokes/refrences that fell flat at their best, and were irritating at their worst. Dictiny's sense of humor does not go beyond "HEY!!!! Remeber THIS thing??? LOL. OMG SO RANDOM, am I rite???XD". I'm talking Schwarzenegger and LotR. The skimming the surface level of muck from over exposed culture.
So as it stands with it's current proformance issues, simplistic hybrid gameplay, and obnoxious writing, I'd actually recomend it at its current early access price of 75% off. Who knows, the gameplay may evolve to such a fantastic level that even a horrendous sense of humor wont bring it down. Or, maybe the writing will improve, but that honestly seems much less likely as Dicetiny's identy seems pretty concrete. There's some real potential here and I'd hate to see it go to waste by the Dev's limiting their creativity and adhering only to existing ip's or out dated refrences.

Edit: UPDATED REVIEW
With the launch of 2.0 there was a reset. I only played for a short while after the update, but I failed to get most of the promised reimbursement for the stuff I earned. I'm not sure if you have to do missions or such, but oh well, I don't play enough anymore for it to bother me though having to grind back to what I was at will take a considerable amount of time which is a little discouraging.
Anywho, I wanted to change up my recommendation for newer players looking to purchase this game.
In short, I do not recommend it. The most refreshing feature used to be the $1 title purchase but the project has become incredibily amitious and based on the content $25 is just too much. Overall, I liked the game when I played it more frequently but lack of content and forum drama caused me to set this on my back burner designated for Early Access games. From my experience with those I gifted the game to, this game is not a lasting game for many people. If you can secure this game for $10, I would recommend at least trying it out.
For those interested, I took the time to write a more informative review below aimed at those looking to purchase the game. To the best of my knowledge all the current information I gave is accurate unless I mentioned otherwise.
While there is more content since the summer when I wrote my last review, the new content along with the accompying controversy did not add a lasting element to the game. There is PvP, PvE, Spaceships (Dog Fighting), and now some NPCs. While that is a decent amount of content, it is still a far cry from the projected plan. Good or bad, there's plenty that hasn't been implemented such as mechs, open universe, or even the ideal Nova City. In short, we do not have the content!
Update schedules are usually monthly to bi-monthly (meaning every 2 months). Projected plans rarely stay on track and content put into updates sometime is changed. I have been both elated and disappointed by this as we recieved new content that wasn't announced and didn't recieve the original, planned content. For instance, I'm sure that numerous people recall that in the 1.7 update, mechs were to be introduced but the idea was shelved  so Developers could fix and tidy up other parts of the game. Even less may recall that 1.5 was supposed to be a mega-update that brought numerous explorable regions and Nova City as well as PvP into the mix during summer 2016 but was ultimately divided into several smaller updates. Overall, there has been decent content progression during the past year of development.
As far as gameplay goes, it is both interesting and lack luster at the same time.
(This was one general section but I spaced it out relating to each element of gameplay so it was a little more readable)
-PvE is basically a "Waves game" where you defend a harvester from dinos and robots as you move about a map. There's a decent amount of customization that you can do for gameplay such as having 2 preset loadouts per each guardian, the ability to actively cycle the camera through Top-Down, 3rd, and 1st Person during gameplay, and gear that increases stats and gives special effects.
-PvP in the game isn't incredibly special and didn't hold my attention so I don't have much to say about how balanced or playable it is. Simply if you want a PvP game, focus on bigger titles like Halo, COD, or Battlefield.
-Spaceship PvP, I glanced over it in game so I do not actually know how well it currently plays if at all. What I do know is that it is currently Dog Fighting and there are 2 different ships.
-Outside of PvE and PvP, you can wander about different areas including a moon spacestation, a cave, a green rocky place, etc (Each area does have a name). NPCs were recently added that will give more missions in future updates with the promise of a full scale campaign story (Looking at past updates, I'm fairly certain this will be implemented sometime around Late March to Late May). You can customize your current guardians set of armor with many different armor pieces and shaders. There is a game shop as well as a premium shop that can be viewed through any terminal.
-Generally, it is more worthwhile farming than shopping at the game shop (though it was not always the case) but it is a nice way off picking up extra crafting materials or equipment 'Rerolls'. The premium shop tends to be on the expensive side in terms of time and money if you don't possess that the discount bonus that Pioneers, Elites, or Founders possess (These do go a long way). 10000000 game currency = 1000 premium currency = 1 dollar = 1/2 shader (some) = 1/5 guardian = roughly 4-5 games ranging from 1-2 hours a piece (Guardian armors and Guardians themselves used to be a packages for 10k premium but were split, I own all of them so I am a little unsure if they were actually split).
There is also a pay shop that has chests which give you the chance at random items including premium items (also expensive in terms of content granted). Early on, the premium currency was fairly simple through some give aways and achievements but give aways were temporarily stopped as well as the currency given through achievements being reduced. The game was stated that it would be pay or play and the best alternative used to be to play, but there is a visible attempt to get players to pay with recent implementations by drastically increasing play times required to unlock content.
-Guardians each have their own special ability and can switch between 2 preset loadouts that vary among each guardian. The level of the game purchased also determines what guardians are unlocked when you start. For instance, I have both the Founder and Elite status so I currently have all 11 or 12 guardians - I don't use them all. (Don't worry I got Founder way back when and I bought Elite when it was on sale). Unfortunately, because the game went through a bumpy F2P back to a title purchase, I am not entirely sure what version unlocks what considering I can't view all the content since I already own the title. If you are interested refer to the forum news and you should find your answer since there was an announcement within the last couple of weeks concerning it. Currently, the lowest title price is $25 (I think you may start out with the Assualt, Support, and Scout from Orion:Prelude but I am not 100%).
As a veteran player I know what each class has and what I like to play, so I could start from scratch and easily unlock the Guardian I want without too much hassle. But for those who are just starting, it takes a decent amount of time to unlock a class that you just found out you don't like to play and more time to find a second class you might like to play.

I love this game. It has adorable slimes, cool upgrades, and TARR SLIMES ARE THE SCARIEST THINGS EVER.
In slime rancher, you play as a young woman named Beatrix LeBeau who travels many lightyears away to capture slimes. In this game, you have a gun. Not a shoot-em-up violent gun, but a vacuum gun. With this vacuum gun you can suck up many resources like veggies, fruits, slime plorts, and most importantly, slimes. You can upgrade this gun to hold many more of those items. You can also buy a jetpack and upgrades for that.
Next, there are the slimes. In this game, there are many different types of slimes. I think at the time of 03/10/16 there are around 9 slimes, including The Tarr. You can collect all of these slimes, except for the Golden Slime and the Tarr. Also, there are larger versions of them, called Largo Slimes.
In this game, there are a wide varitity of items. There are many fruits, veggies, and meats (mostly chickens). All of the slimes have a favorite food, and only eat one type of food. An example is the Rock Slime eats all veggies, but its favorite veggie is the Heart Beet.
Next, is the habitats. In Slime Rancher, you keep your slimes in corrals. There are also gardens, ponds (which you use to keep the water slime in), coops, and incinerators. There are also many upgrades for these, like auto-feeder and auto plort collector.
Lastly, is expansions. In this game, you save up money you make from plorts to buy expansions to the map. Don’t worry, it’s not real money. At the moment (03/10/16) there are 2 expansions. I’ll leave the rest of the secrets of the game for you to find.
Now, since the basic information is out of the way, it’s time for some pros and cons.
Pros
-Fun to Play
-Pretty Graphics
-Simple
-ADORABLE
-Many Upgrades
-You Want to Keep Playing
-It Makes You Feel Powerful
-Semi-Cheap Price
Cons
-Semi-Expensive Price
-I Pretty Much Beat The Game In 6 Hours (By Beat I Mean I Got All The Upgrades and Captured All The Slimes)
-FRICKEN TARR SLIMES (Just Kidding)
-No Multiplayer
There are not very many cons, but they are still ones to keep in mind.
Conclusion: I feel that this game is very fun, cute, and entertaining, but it only has a limited amount of gameplay and it needs some further updates. I recommend you get this game, as they have announced new slimes, multiplayer, and expansions. You may only play for five or six hours, but when the new update comes out, it will just get better.

Currently a good candidate for best fighting game ever made, even in this competitive time of good 2D fighters.
The character variety is beyond what I've seen elsewhere.  Take the movement mechanics, for one example: I-no's regular dash lifts her off the ground, allowing her to access her air moves easily while approaching; Slayer teleports short distances instead of dashing; fitting his manly character, Johnny's forward dash is longer than his backwards hop; even Sin's pretty average backdash is animated as a backflip using his staff.  People run, jump, fly and teleport ninja-style all over the place.  Stylin.  There's a lot of personality here, and there's bound to be a character you like among the mix of heavy metal and anime inspired designs.  Sol has a giant belt buckle with the word FREE scratched into it, and his bandana says ROCK YOU.  The visuals and music are top tier.
The online features are very well done.  The lobbies are like little arcades; you walk around as your avatar, type in chat, and spectate or jump on one of the little arcade machines and join somebody for a battle.  It's awesome, you can easily jump off a machine and watch somebody else's fight to relax until you're ready to go again.  Best lobby system for a fighting game that I've ever seen.  Being able to switch to spectating right away helps to dim the pain of getting rekt (many beginners aren't brave enough to try an online lobby - those people tend to stay beginners.  Be brave, and don't let damaged pride stop you from fighting to improve!).  It really hearkens back to ye olde arcade days.
I can't explain it in terms of frame data, but where combos in BlazBlue felt 'restrictive' to me, I find that the gattling combos here tend to be more freeform and custom once you figure out what-links-into-what.  That's not to say certain characters aren't extremely execution-heavy; try Chipp or Millia if you're a combo pro.  Of course, certain chains only work on characters of the right height/size, so you sometimes have to adapt your 'maximal' combos to suit the character you're fighting.  You don't just learn your own character: you learn how your character deals with the other 20-some characters.  You do that by playing, watching, and maybe doing research if you really want to crack a certain character who's beating you.  Ya gotta figure out what your own good moves are, too!
There's a lot of casual content to enjoy (an entertaining story mode, the usual arcade modes and color/gallery unlockables, etc.) and an incredibly rich tutorial system (tons of challenges to teach you the systems and get your muscle memory started).  There's even a 'stylish' control mode for people who need some time understand the flow of a fighting game, and who want to do some flashy moves without having to learn complex inputs right away.
But, if you really want to get good at this game, you have to be prepared to lose a lot in PvP.  That's just the nature of a fighting game: the journey from noob to pro is the content.  Instead of grinding an RPG character, you're grinding your brain, reflexes and muscle memory.  This is real.  You may face one or two people who have been doing that since the original Guilty Gear about 20 years ago.  You're going to want to join a Discord channel or other community hub so you can absorb other peoples' experience and complain together about Raven.  Only Raven players like Raven.

After playing hundreds of matches on PC, PS4 and the odd arcade match, I can confidently say this is the most fun I've had in a fighting game in my life.
Wonderful characters, art and presentation. An attention to detail I've seldom seen, and it comes through in every aspect of the game. Between the intros, outros, overdrives, instakill cinematics, character lines/interactions and godly rock/metal OST, I don't see how anybody can make the case for this game not looking and sounding amazing.
The gameplay is absolutely fantastic. Between the myriad of universal mechanics and the wacky character specific stances/setups/quirks, you will be able to play this game for hundreds of hours and still find yourself saying "Wait, that WORKS?" on some matches.
The only downside I can think of is that this game has basically turned me into a Jehovah's witness. You will start trying to get everybody you know to play this game. Usually with little success, as the super steep learning curve and anime aesthetic will put most people off. BUY THIS GAME.

Dark souls 2 Is the next instalment in the demon souls game series and whoo boy does it surprise you. Compared to Dark Souls the second instalment is much more easier to get in to, all of the enemies are more balanced toward starting out, but yet I died several times because of the absolute stupidity of my own actions. The first time I died was because I accidentally tapped the controller the other way just a little too much and ended up walking off a cliff. The last time I died before making this video...I walked backwards off a cliff while fighting giant guardians...note to self keep an eye on cliffs.

Regardless the story is as deep and as vague as it was in dark souls, but it's better explained through visual means more then outright telling you what the hell is going on nor what your overall goal is. The only goal you know of thus far is to prevent yourself becoming a hollow and meet the king, or this is what I understood so far, I'm still playing through the game and I really don't want to spoil anything for new players, finding out the story is half of these games anyway.

Combat is more fluid then it was in the predecessors like said it's easier to get in to, but just like it's predecessors it's hard to master and more often then not bad timing in fights or biting too much you can't chew will end up killing you rather efficiently.

The hollow/Undead versus humanity aspect is also more different then it was in dark souls. As I've understood (I could be wrong) there are things called Human Effigies that can be used to turn yourself back to human and negating all the health loss you've gained while dying in Hollow form and you can use this same item and burn it in bonfires to disable online interactions preventing people from invading your world. Now I have not been invaded yet which could be due to the game being released a few hours ago, but not sure if being hollow stops people from invading like it was in dark souls, just in case I usually play as a hollow, unless I die enough times.

Like I mentioned before I'm still playing through the game and I'm enjoying it majorly and anyone who is a fan of the demon souls and dark souls games, I would say this is a good buy, it might not be as unforgiving as dark souls, but it's still enjoyable none the less.

Update: Okay so we got more content stuff now against all odds the "cutesy" art is actually growing on me ONLY because it is used to highlight the parody heavy theme presnet in this EA access title.
Not a thumbs up at this point however b/c when it comes to strategic gameplay there's not really alot too it unfortuantely....BUT there have been some changes and the developer's seem willing to listen to feedback and adjust even the core gameplay (assuming I am understanding the updates they give correctly) mechanic may improve or develop in some way not yet apparent.
At the moment this game comes off as couple of new shoes on the much played, loved, hated, and all time classic boardgame, Monopoly. Primarily it's a game of chance though some strategic application will improve your odds. As such I will primiraly being making comparision contrasts to help review this concept.
One of my complaints is that in tweaking the Monopoly formula Dicetiny replaces purchasing property tiles with placing minions that can be defeated/removed/stolen and the result is a bit underwhelming. It removes the decisions between keeping resources or spending them in hopes of at least a small future or short term benefit but with the possibly of a huge payoff in the long run feel. That very decisions is what makes Monoploy somewhat interesting.  I say somewhat interseting concept because while the decisions set in front of you will change based on the dice roll/RNG/Random element of a particular game of Monopoly the overall strategy of each game is essentially the same (focusing on purchasing properties in a few key areas and not in others). I believe this is a result of having a fixed "permenant" gameboard that the elements are subject to is partially (maybe entirely?) to blame here and Dicetiny forgoes that particular dilema with the ability to randomize the board to  and the last half of each game tends to be a long jog to an inevitable conclusion.
So in short form for this Monopoly variation the non-permenancy (totally a word I'm sure) spin on purchasing obstacles (properites in Monopoly and Units or Minions in Dicetiny) seems to accomplish the task of making the game less vanilla. Steam World Dig reminds me of this old Xbox Live Indie game called Miner Dig Deep. They both have the same basic idea. Dig for valuable minerals, return to the surface to sell off your gains, buy new equipment & supplies, repeat. It's a simple concept but it's addictive and entertaining. Steamworld Dig adds to this concept and creates a very nice game.
The goal of the game is to make your way to the bottom of an ancient underground labyrinth. Mostly you'll be digging your way through, however you'll make occasional detours to collect special upgrades. These upgrades include the ability to dig through rocks, fire projectiles, and eventually even double-jump. It's kinda comparable to Metroid, since you can use the upgrades to find better stuff in previous areas. There are also various creatures to deal with. There are a handful of ways to deal with them aside from just using your pickax. This game is really combat-oriented though, just consider it another obstacle in the way of your loot.
Steamworld Dig is a very well-paced game. Aside from monsters, there are also traps and other issues that crop as your scour the depths. There might even be times where you can't find a way back up. Unless you can find a teleporter(or brought one with you), the only alternative will be very costly repairs. Getting crushed by rocks is also a thing that can happen. Really though, this is an easy game. It's very much something that you put in to relax for a bit.
Not to say that this game doesn't have any challenge. There are end-game rankings as well as a variety of ways for you to challenge yourself. Maybe on your next play-through you can skimp on the health upgrades, or devise that perfect route to get through the game as fast as possible. For some one trip through the labyrinth is enough, but Steamworld Dig does offer more, and the good controls and playablity make for welcome return trips.

I wasn't sure about this game, I read a ton of bad reviews and didn't give it much hope. many people are crying about lag, game crashes, it is just a copy of Warz, why would you make pve servers. etc... Blah blah blah... First, if you are playing this on anything then less then the minimum requirements then don't complain about lag. I play with a guy that only has 2 gigs of memory and has an old GTX470 graphics card and his FPS was in the 70s most of the time with no lag at all. Yes there will be game crashes, its a game and its "early alpha" or what ever they want to call it. My gaming group played Aftermath all weekend and never had a game crash issue so take that anyway you want it. So what if it is just a copy of WarZ, it gives us everything other zombie games do not give you, Dayz anyone?.. Then there are the big babies that don't understand why they are giving us PVE servers. here is a simple piece of advice for you people crying about PVE... DONT PLAY ON A PVE SERVER IF YOU DONT LIKE PVE... see how simple that is? There are pvp servers in this game so find one and shut up already.
Now for the things that some of us that like this game might be interested in. It is growing and getting better... Simple as that. The crafting is easy, the zombies are plentiful and can be overwhelming at times thought they really are pretty easy to outrun. The graphics are ok, not great but ok. The grouping feature works but there has to be a better way then having to type (/ginvite "playername") and (/gaccept "playername") kind of clunky but it does work. also loading the weapon is not as easy as it could be either... having to equip the pistol, then press f6 to load it is kind of stupid. then there is the shear amount of crap loot in the game. very little in the way of good stuff, but hey if you need a rope coil you are all set.
In the end this game is good, not great but good. we had a ton of fun playing it and when we are able to build a base it will be even more fun. if you want to try it, go for it, it is free and wont cost you anything. if you are one of those that hate this game and have nothing but complaints, STOP PLAYING IT. its free and you lost nothing by giving it a try so stop crying and shut up about it already.

Xenonauts wants to be the direct spiritual successor to UFO: Enemy Unknown by remaking the original with some fidelity. In combat, soldiers move and shoot according to a system based on time units identical (?) to the original; so the combat is pretty much like you would expect, except there is a directional cover system implemented, oh, and suppression. Air combat is no longer 1v1 and now you can directly control your aircraft, a mini game that can become tedious with time, but a welcome change nevertheless. I prefer the art style of old X-Com, Xenonauts looks a bit ugly to me. I didn’t play this game a lot but from what I saw the game has its own take on a lot of little things. One thing that stood out and I liked is the introduction of shields. I think the game is OK but I wasn’t impressed with anything, and in the end I just didn’t find it exciting to play.

You have a lot more graphics options, the resolution is supported up to and including 1440p, the keys are rebindable, the game has upped the texture quality substantially and FPS maxes out at 60. Even lesser computers seem to run this game fine.
I've played the Souls games a lot, including Demon's Souls. I've got over 100 hours played of the PS3 version of Dark Souls 2 and despite earlier fears of comments from From Software that the game would be more accessible (ie more casual) the game is actually still rock hard and even if you think you know every nook and cranny of the previous Souls games, this game still throws a lot of new challanges at you. You will still die. A lot.
One of the gripes I had with the game was that despite it reportedly having 40 bosses, most of them are just humanoid-shaped dudes, brandishing some form of sword and shield combination. Some boss battles are really inventive however and I would despite aformentioned gripe, wholeheartedly recommend Dark Souls 2 to anyone in need of a proper challenge.

I am absolutely speechless.
This is the most worthy sequel Dishonored could have possibly gotten. One of my top 3 games of all time, played through multiple times on PC and console, now has a proper continuation.
EDIT 11/13/16: Just finished my first lethal run-through of the game as Emily. My review still stands. So much creativity and love went into making this game, and it shows.
EDIT 11/21/16: The performance issues plaguing the game have been fixed. Runs like butter on my GTX 970 and i7 4790k, 16GB of RAM. Constant 60FPS at 1080p with no stuttering running on Very High / Ultra.
The game itself:
Every gameplay element has been expanded on, powers now have upgrade tiers to let you choose specifics, swordfight mechanics have been improved, stealth has been improved, and the visuals, animations, and story are stunning so far. The voice acting is top notch, and the new chaos system, along with more options for non-lethal combat (even in full alert situations) allow for more diverse and fun approaches to scenarios. Emily and her new abilities are incredibly refreshing if you've played Dishonored 1 to death with Corvo's abilities like I have. That being said, Corvo also has some new improvements and upgrades that make his new gameplay equally as enthralling. The AI is incredibly smart this time around, as far as I can tell, and I haven't been detected in any scenario that wasn't entirely my fault. Hard work clearly went into the genius level design throughout this entire game. There's so much fun and freedom to be had. I can't recommend it more. After 4 playthroughs, I'm still finding new and interesting methods as well as secrets and alternate paths to the story.
I am overjoyed with this game. It's everything Dishonored would have been in a perfect world.

So far so good. I really enjoyed my first play through. There is no tutorial, they just kinda throw you in there and you learn on the go. For people who have played Hearthstone you will pick it up a bit faster. There is a game guild that helps.
Again, I must stress that this game is in Beta and there is a lot more Fakedice has planned from what I have seen so as far as the beta goes I am impressed and can not wait to see more.

So I heard about this game through Letigress' stream. My understanding is she partnered up with the developers in order to help promote the game, which is neat. So lets get into why I DO reccomend this game...
The style is very remincent of Hearthstone. The cards look slightly similar but the style is VERY different. I mean, for starters, its a board game. Games take anywhere between 5-15 minutes for a round, which I think is perfect. There is a fair amount of strategy that goes into a match. For $5, I think it is totally worth giving this game a try and seeing where the developers take it! Now... Here is what I'd like to see from the game...
-MULTIPLAYER! This game needs to let me play against my friends. That's like 80% of the appeal. I've already beat all the bots. Give me new game modes. This should be the developers first priority.
-Card variety. Right now the starter deck gets stale after 3-5 hours. There is very little you can do with it at the moment. This game needs 100+ cards to REALLY start to be something special.
-More characters. This is a given and the developers know this. I'm excited to see what they come up with. The abilities of the NPCs you can play seem neat.
-Let the text and dialogue move at the player's pace. Create like a "Next" arrow when interactions and stuff are happening. Everything moves so fast right now and I missed a lot of it when I first started.
-New boards. The board now is cool, but I'd like more stuff to happen on it and in the future even have different boards that aren't as simple as a single square. Maybe something that can accomodate more than two players?
That's all I have for now. I'll update as the developers do. You should get this game. It is cheap and a lot of fun! I only have 1.4 hours shows while I write this, but played offline for 5ish hours. I'll probably play 5 or so more on this patch then wait for updates. Thank you to Letigress for turning me on to this! :)
Cheers.

The way the turns are set up is alot like monopoly, you roll dice and can land on;
monsters (chose to fight or hire them to work for you),
community chest type spaces,
a dungeon (beat the monster and add it too your hand),
a store to buy a card where you can buy a card to add to your hand
and another square where you can buy upgrades for your heros stats
also after each lap you gain 100 gold and you get 50 gold for each monster you kill along the way.

Video version of this review:
Super Meat Boy is a platform game with a fairly high level of difficulty. Your girlfriend, Bandage Girl, has been captured by Dr. Fetus. Hey, whenever you’re hungry, do you yell, “Feed us”? And when you get tired of walking, you sit down and rest your “Feet-us”? Alright, I’m out of fetus jokes.
You have to do a lot of quick and tricky platforming to get around a bunch of obstacles. There are all sorts of stuff to avoid, like saw, lasers, needles, monsters, and so on. Don’t expect your first time playing to be a cinch. You will die… a lot. Every time you beat a level, they show a replay, showing every attempt you’ve ever made all at the same time. I died so many times on one level, I broke the replay, and had to exit to the map in order to continue on.
As angry as I have gotten, the bosses are actually quite fun. They’re very challenging, but still possible to beat. I kept getting hand cramps from all the intense platforming I was pulling off. I sure had one hell of a time with the race at the end of the Salt Factory. You have to escape as quickly as you can before the salt can reach you. No thanks, Dr. Fetus, I’ve already been plenty salty at this game. So anyway, I spent a total of thirty minutes on this level, and boy, did I get mad. But it wasn’t until a while after I beat it that I started to realize how somewhat fun it was. Because as hard as it was, and with all the times I kept saying it was stupid, it was still fair. You just have to find the best method for speed.
In some of the levels there are bandages to pick up. I haven’t really bothered to pick them up, because they are difficult to get. Besides, all they really do is allow you to get new skins. You can also get new skins in other ways. I got Commander Video from one of the warp zones in the first world. He moves slower than Meat Boy, but he can hover in the air if you hold the jump button. But playing as him didn’t really work out for me, so I switched back to Meat Boy.
Some of the really intense platforming can be really fun to do. But others are not, especially when you have to do them over and over, and you can’t figure out a way to get past some areas. I’ve certainly had my fill of rage, especially in one of the Hell levels where you have to ride a platform and avoid being hit by these flying mouth things. But I have died so many times from them, I literally was screaming. But it wasn’t just that that made me angry, what made me even angrier is this one glitch where I keep dying while the platform is moving under a narrow space. This has happened several times, and ONLY in the Hell chapter.
When it comes to glitches, the Rapture chapter has been such a problem that I haven’t actually beaten it, and ended up rage-quitting. There’s a level I had no choice but to skip because I kept on glitching through the descending platform, and landing right on the saws. There was no way to avoid the glitchiness of this level, so I went somewhere else. There was even a level where I ran straight into the floor, like, I was literally in the floor.
I’ve seen forum threads talking about the exact same problem that made me rage-quit: unresponsive jumping. This is a problem I’ve had throughout the game, but it was never as bad as it was in the Rapture chapter. Probably 90% of my deaths in this chapter were a result of unresponsive jumps. This problem actually ruins the game, because you only need to play a certain amount of levels to fight the boss, but with the levels I actually had to skip because of the broken jumping controls, and that one elevator glitch, there is no way I’m gonna be able to get there.
I can’t really say I recommend this game 100%, solely because of the glitches and jumping problem. But I think I can still recommend it because it is actually a lot of fun to play. I’m not usually one for games of high difficulty, but I will say that I think this is a great challenge for anyone who loves platformers as much as I do.

Steam World Dig reminds me of this old Xbox Live Indie game called Miner Dig Deep. They both have the same basic idea. Dig for valuable minerals, return to the surface to sell off your gains, buy new equipment & supplies, repeat. It's a simple concept but it's addictive and entertaining. Steamworld Dig adds to this concept and creates a very nice game.
The goal of the game is to make your way to the bottom of an ancient underground labyrinth. Mostly you'll be digging your way through, however you'll make occasional detours to collect special upgrades. These upgrades include the ability to dig through rocks, fire projectiles, and eventually even double-jump. It's kinda comparable to Metroid, since you can use the upgrades to find better stuff in previous areas. There are also various creatures to deal with. There are a handful of ways to deal with them aside from just using your pickax. This game is really combat-oriented though, just consider it another obstacle in the way of your loot.
Steamworld Dig is a very well-paced game. Aside from monsters, there are also traps and other issues that crop as your scour the depths. There might even be times where you can't find a way back up. Unless you can find a teleporter(or brought one with you), the only alternative will be very costly repairs. Getting crushed by rocks is also a thing that can happen. Really though, this is an easy game. It's very much something that you put in to relax for a bit.
Not to say that this game doesn't have any challenge. There are end-game rankings as well as a variety of ways for you to challenge yourself. Maybe on your next play-through you can skimp on the health upgrades, or devise that perfect route to get through the game as fast as possible. For some one trip through the labyrinth is enough, but Steamworld Dig does offer more, and the good controls and playablity make for welcome return trips.

This totally reinvigorated the "Digging around" genre for me. I played a ton of Terraria when it first dropped and a whole bunch of others have felt like shallow immitators, but this is confident in its own concept and just a blast.

SteamWorld Dig has a lot of polish. The controlls are tight and feel good when you are playing. The world is simple and elegent. Graphically it has a great look. I enjoyed my time until about 3/4 of the way through. About half way through something started eating at me. When I was about 75% of the way through it hit me. This game has nothing to it.

You mine for ore, you sell your ore, you buy stuff. You are not hunting down recipes, or farming for specific ingrediants. You are not looking for specific enemy spawns and hoping for the correct loot drop. The secret areas might as well have a glowing neon sign pointing to it. The game is extremely simple and linear.

It feels like a glorified flash game. A well done flash game, but even still. This could have been a really fantastic game. It just needed more depth.

This game is an electronic version of the pen and graph paper game "Dots and Boxes". Most people in the US (and probably elsewhere) have played this game as children.
Unfortunately, there are zero twists added to the basic game. It's just that game you play on graph paper with nothing new added to it. There are no original ideas or twists to make the game interesting. The only difference between "levels" is the shape of the game board, so the levels don't get any harder as you progress (the decision procedure gets a little harder but is still terrible, see below).
This game has no AI whatsoever. That would be fine if the decision procedure used to choose the computer's moves made the game challenging, but the procedural choices fail to look more than two moves ahead. Whoever programmed the decision procedure doesn't know how to play this game properly and doesn't know what AI is. It's laughably easy and doesn't get harder as you go. I stuck it out in the hopes it would get more challenging, but it's just boring and slow because the game boards are unnecessarily large.

I’m not going to accuse OddPlanet of being a Limbo-clone, since the developers already acknowledge that that game was a major inspiration for this title and it’s fairly obvious if you even just look at a single screenshot of the game, so I don’t want to dwell on it.
The controls feel rather floaty and imprecise. Jumping does not always work the way I intended and the throwing mechanic can be a source for frustration, since the protagonist always throws her rocks in an arc and you always have to go back and forth to the pile of rocks to get another one if you miss a shot. The challenges the game provides are repeated dozens of times. Sneaking past enemies is basically your only MO in this game and there are two mechanics to avoid them. One is to simply hide on a dark patch of background image for enemies who can see you in the open and react to when you running around, and the other is to avoid stepping on the little spiders whenever the larger, blind spiders are on the prowl. That’s basically all there’s to it.
The puzzles almost always boil down to “explore the environment until you find the object that lets you overcome the current obstacle”. At times you’ve got to drag around items in order to form stepping stones, but for the most part you’ll not end up solving any puzzles, just sneaking your way past identical enemies ad nauseam.
There are hints of a story here but the game is too short to really expand upon it, with a fairly cheap ending that tries too hard to tug at your heart strings. And yet, even with the short runtime, I still felt like it dragged out its content too much. All in all, I’m not sure I can recommend this one.

Oddplanet is one of those games that is very similar to LIMBO, they say that is inspired, some say that is a rip off. But has some elements that separate it from limbo which I will adress on this review.
Gameplay
The gameplay is similar on LIMBO in terms of being a platform puzzle, but while in LIMBO it relies on jumping, pushing/pulling/grabbing stuff and in gravity maniputation, this game relies on jumping, taking items, and sneaking in this hostile world in order to proceed in the levels.
One thing that is neat about this game is the level design of the puzzles, while not complex and if you pay attention you can solve them easily, they're well thought and in some cases you need to get the items of a certain area in order to solve another area. The bad thing about this is that because the protagonist gives her thoughts about the situation this basically spoils the fun of the puzzles themselves because the "hints" can either be either helpful to blatantly telling you how to solve it.
So it's a mix bag of clever puzzles and obvious stuff. Most of the levels are lineal, with the 3rd level being the only one with an some exploration.
Controls
They clunky but they're manegable, but i have an issue when i wanted to  run and jump because when I pressed up and then left it jumped up and not left, maybe it's because of the engine they used but it's still a problem.
I remember the controls in LIMBO being better so if they still work on the game they should fix the controls like the other coments mentioned.
Story
It's not something special, it's just the adventure of a girl who went off to a strange world by a broken ship and she explores the world while writing on her journal at the end of a level about her life or her thoughts about the adventure so far.
And while the story in this game is not vry important the adventure itself can give you a certain feeling, especially in the end chapter when...
Graphics
Similar to limbo most of the characters are black, but the worlds themselves are colorful and some of the enemies are colorful too, which can be a little inconsistent untill you notice that the colors are necesary to solve puzzles.
Soundtrack
Atmospheric and bland, it does serve it's purpose and creates the atmosphere of the world but it's not something you'll be actively look forward to, except when you want some music to study on the final exam.
Overall
The game is fine for what it is even if it's very short for my likings. But if you want to solve puzzles, while they're definitely better alternatives in the market, like portal 1 and 2, if you can get this one on a sale then go for it because they might challenge you.

Das Wichtigste in Kürze:
Das Spiel ist vor allem für sentimentalere und fantasiereichere Menschen gedacht oder für jene, die sich an Sentimentalerem und/oder für etwas (dark) Fantasy begeistern. Das liegt daran, dass der Fokus des Spieles auf einer nett anzusehenden Kulisse und schöner, aber düsterer Atmosphäre liegt. Das kleine Mädchen, das man spielt,
steht ebenfalls im Mittelpunkt. Sie ist neugierig, freundlich und emotional. Daher ist das Spiel meiner Meinung nach auch für Personen gedacht, die sich einigermaßen in das Mädchen hineinversetzen können, oder sich mit ihr identifizieren können.
Zu bedenken gilt aber, dass die Reise im Spiel eine kurze ist. Ich habe für meinen ersten Spieldurchlauf nur etwas mehr als eine Stunde gebraucht, allerdings kam ich auch sehr gut durch und hing nur bei einem kleinem Rätsel etwas fest. Ich prognostiziere also eine durchschnittliche Spielzeit von 1-2 h.
Weiteres:
Der Sound insgesamt ist etwas leise. Mit Headset und etwas mehr Lautstärke wirkt das Spiel gleich viel stimmungsvoller.
Die Steuerung ist am Anfang gewöhnungsbedürftig, aber akzeptabel. Wenn man einmal damit umgehen kann, geht die Steuerung einfacher von der Hand. Gerade am Anfang gibt es aber ein paar 'schwierigere' Jump'n Run Stellen, die es im weiteren Spielverlauf eher gar nicht mehr gibt. Das hemmt zu Beginn unter Umständen den Spielspaß.
Die Bewegungsanimationen des Mädchens sind akzeptabel, aber dennoch etwas grob.
Die Rätsel sind recht einfach, aber das störte mich kein bisschen.
Ich spielte das Spiel zwei mal durch. Für mich, denn auch ich bin emotionaler und fantasiereicher, war das Erlebns jedes mal angenehm. Dabei ist mir auch gar nicht so wichtig, dass das Spiel so kurz ist. Wiederspielwert hat das Spiel "spielerisch" zwar nicht, aber ich zum Beispiel erfreue mich an der schön gestalteten Spielewelt und freue mich jedes Mal unheimlich über den kleinen, süßen Pepito ^.^ ,sodass ich es mit etwas zeitlichem Abstand immer mal wieder spielen könnte.
Das Spiel insgesamt ist recht düster gehalten. Ich stufe es als Dark Fantasy & Sci-fi ein.
Wie die Geschichte endet, finde ich gar nicht gut. Das hintert mich aber nicht, das Spiel als solches und die Handlung bis zum Ende hin sehr schön zu finden.
Ich empfehle dringend, die englischen Untertitel zu wählen. Zunächst wählte ich deutsche Untertitel. Diese wirkten wie von Google Übersetzer und waren teilweise recht unverständlich
Dafür, dass im Grunde nur 1-3 Personen an dem Spiel gearbeitet haben, ist es gut gelungen finde ich.
Ich mag den Credits-Song :3 und ich würde mir wünschen, dass das Spiel in irgendeiner Form weiter ginge.
Ich mag es nicht, Punkte zu verteilen, weil Reviews vor allem persönliche Empfindungen sind. Daher stufe >ich< es als ein gutes Spiel ein.
--------
Most important parts first:
The game is suited primarily for the more sentimental and fanciful ones or for those thrilled by rather sentimental and/or (dark) fantasy. That is because the game is focussed on a picturesque scenery and a pretty yet dark atmosphere. The small girl you play is central, too. She is curious, friendly and emotional. Thus, the game is in my opinion also suited for people able to somewhat empathize with the girl or identify with her.
But it needs to be pointed out that the game's journey is a short one. My first game run-through took me just a little more than an hour, however I got through very well and only got stuck at a small riddle. I therefore predict an average playtime of 1-2 h.
Furthermore:
The sound in overall is a little low. Using headset and some more volume quckly make the game seem moodier.
The control takes some getting used to, but is acceptable. Once you got your head around it, you find the control no trouble. Specially in the beginning, there are some 'more difficult' jump'n'run parts which are near non-existent in later gameplay. This might hamper the fun in the beginning.
The moving animations of the girl are acceptable, but still a little unsubtle.
The riddles are fairly easy,but that did not bother me at all.
I played through the game two times. For me, being the more emotional and fanciful kind, the experience  was pleasant each time. It did not matter too much to me that the game was so short. There is not much replay value "play-wise", yet I for example am delighted by the nicely arranged game world and chuckle every time terrificly over the small, sweet Pepito ^.^, so that I could repeatedly play it again after a while.
The game in overall is kept in a rather dark mood. I rank it dark fantasy & sci-fi.
I really do not like the way the story ends. It did not however compromise my appreciation of the game itself and its plot until the end.
I urgently suggest to choose the English subtitles. At first, I chose the German ones. Those appealed as if done by Google translator and were quite unintelligible in some parts.
Considering there were basically just 1-3 people working on the game, they did a good job on it, I think.
I like the credits song :3 and I'd love to see the story continue in some way.
I do not like giving out points, since reviews are mostly personal perception. Hence >I< rate it a good game.
It's a nice game but extremely short and sad without proper ending. It would be good to have a sequel which closes the story.

Superior to Sign in every aspect and one of the very best fighting games of this generation.
The gamplay has been fine tuned to near perfection. Blitz Shield is much easier to use, Side Dusts are now a thing, less input delay, even better online, lots of balance changes to help close the gaps between tiers and numerous features that cater to both hardcore and casual fans.
Blitz Charge is probably my favorite addition as it not only makes the Blitz mechanic easier to use (at the cost of less reward), but it allows for some intense mindgames. The overhauled Side Dusts are amazing too, giving players even more ways to punish their opponents in the corner and opening up a plethora of new combos and strats.
If you are completely new to Guilty Gear, fear not, for Revelator has lots of in-depth tutorials (Most of them from Sign, but the main tutorial is brand new!) to help teach newcomers all about the game and even a Stylish control scheme. Combos too hard? Struggling to learn command inputs? Why, for only 20% less health pick up the Stylish type and you'll be good to go! The in-game encyclopedia from Sign has also been carried over and updated with entries related to all the new stuff in Revelator.
All the new extras are amazing too. Currently I have 600+ hours, but a good chunk of those were spent just messing around in Gallery, Story and Digital Figure. A lot of the online stuff is sadly carried over from Sign, but there's stil a lot of new content to be unlocked! The VA interviews were definitely my favorite thing to unlock. It was really nice listening to them share their thoughts on the game.
That said, you're gonna need the Rev 2 DLC, if you wanna play online, since everybody has moved on to that version. You can still ask for matches, as long as folks are willing to switch back to the previous version.
A must buy. Let's enjoy a great showtime!
