Intro
Plastiland is a side-scroller puzzle-platformer that combines creative clay graphics, playful bouncy music, and a challenging yet open level design to deliver an engaging experience that will surely captivate puzzle-platformer enthusiasts.
Graphics
The graphics are akin to a sort of clay animation like you’d see in Wallace and Gromit. That’s where the comparison ends though, where Wallace and Gromit may appear as bleak and bland in terms of the colors, Plastiland’s colors are bright, cheery, optimistic, varied, and heavily contrasting. I thoroughly enjoyed the graphics, it was a trip down memory lane yet a refreshing experience that diverges from the graphics in many puzzle-platformers on Steam today.
Sound
The sound is pretty cool to me, it was probably the biggest surprise of the entire game to me. The music is fun and playful – reminds me of the type of music you would hear at a state fair. It definitely adds to the overall atmosphere of the game. The sound effects are another strong suit and happen to fairly accurate. For example, if you let one of your spheres hit the ground, you hear a “SPLAT!” and it correctly corresponds to the splat that you see on the screen.
Gameplay
The gameplay is fairly straightforward. The player must guide a finite amount of spherical creatures that are constantly moving from Point A (A Green Pipe) to Point B (A Red Pipe). The player controls these spherical creatures by changing them into a variety of forms in order to get them past a variety of obstacles in the level.
There are eight forms to be exact. The first form is the Roller, which is the main character. The second form is the Bomber, which disrupts and explodes in the environment after 3 seconds. The third form is the Crusher, which makes a vertical passage. The fourth form is the Crawler, which can crawl up on any wall. The fifth form is the Blocker, stop any other ball. The sixth form is the Builder, which expands to make a passage. The seventh form is the Chewer, which makes a horizontal passage. The eighth form is the Jumper, which can fall from any height. The player starts with a limited number of uses for each form. Each use allows the player to change one sphere into that specific form. The number of uses for each form varies and changes depending on the level which is where part of the challenge comes in. You have to make lemons out of lemonade.
The gameplay requires you to think outside of the box and repeat levels constantly.
The final note that I would add for the gameplay would be that beating levels is sort of similar to the ultra-popular mobile game “Cut the Rope” – the more spheres you get in the red pipe, the higher number of stars you will receive upon the completion of the level. You can receive anywhere from 1, 2, or 3 stars upon completion of a level.
Overall Thoughts
This is a great little under-the-radar game as far as I am concerned. It’s a puzzle-platformer that does its job well. It’s fairly original when compared to many puzzle-platformers, you’re not going to find that repetitive 8-bit or 16-bit retro aesthetic that seems to be all the rage on Steam these days. However, you are going to get a cheerful, optimistic atmosphere that is highlighted by a rich, warm soundtrack that permeates through your side-scrolling form-changing gameplay.

Plastiland is a puzzle-platformer game what can remind for us a classical Lemmings. Your goal in the game transport little clay creatures from the start point to the target point. For this you also should sometimes transform they to the other ones. This game can get a lot of fun for many hours for you,  and if you have little children,  I think  they will absolutely love this game.The game has a great tutorial, so if you go through it, you will know all features of each transformation, preparing you for the game. At the moment the game features 48 levels, but in the future there'll be even more. The graphics looks amazing, all elements of the game are handmade and all the creatures and  the game world are very cute. The music and sound are also really pleasant.

So my verdict

+many levels
+nice musics an sounds
+cute and beautiful handmade graphics
+can be enjoyable for each and every age

-achievements

So Plastiland is a nice puzzle game with unique handmade graphic. This game mostly for children’s, but can be enjoyable at all ages. At the moment the price may be too high, but if the game get a achievements and trading cards, the value can rise in a lot of people's eyes. If you want something for your children's, I think buying this game for them is a good decision.

You can ride around at 150 on the motorway crashing into russians in multiplayer, or you can buckle down and build a trucking empire! This game would be pretty good even if the empire and business management aspect weren't in it. There's a real sense of weight. You definitely feel like you're controlling something big and heavy when you're hauling a 120K pound Rex Tex, contrasted with how free it feels with no trailer or a light 10K pound trailer of used packaging. There are an extensive number of trucks, and all the trucks are customizable. The world and the trucks look and sound really good, and there are visual delights throughout (Sunrises, sunsets, hot air balloons, cruise ships out on the water, fields of golden sunflowers, etc. etc.) And they nailed the time element, neither too slow in reference to reality nor too fast.
But the game doesn't end just by buying your favorite truck, customizing it up, and driving it around delivering different trailers. You can hire employees, fire employees, and manage a trucking empire spanning across Europe. You can challenge yourself by trying to get your delivered trailer parked in just the right spot. Customize not only your truck, but all the trucks in your fleet. Discover 100% of the map. Increase your skills to take on hazardous cargo, fragile cargo, valuable cargo, and more. You can even play your songs or set up Internet radio in-game.

Revised review 2017-01-01.
I've done two playthroughs and do like the product. It's not flawless, but it's a great creation which even breaks a bit of some new ground here and there. I'll stick with my thumbs-down, though, because of the too-low-FOV idiocy that is just inexcusable. I am fed up with the damn trouble stupid developers keep forcing me through, so thumbs-down is what they get, period.
Also, really: DO. NOT. PRE-ORDER. No matter how great a company's products had been in the past. Eidos Montreal / Square Enix fkd us over with surprise-episodic format consumable-preorder-bonus "Deus Ex: Mankind Divided" and all its bugs, now Arkane Studios did the same with their buggy release (mouse speed was bound to FPS, which is unthinkably wrong and also impossible if the game is tested for like 5 minutes, showing the pre-order "Out the door you go! No matter if done!" attitude). We are the beta-testers. If we pre-order. Also, 1.7 months after release, the game was already available for half the price at Saturn Germany, a media store which usually has quite higher prices than discounted Steam games. Just wait, ok.
The FOV slider only goes from 65 to 110 (horizontal; seems to become wider on screens that have wider aspect ratio, so at least there's that), and editing the config file's FOV variable outside this range does not have effect. So, as per my new
, this game gets a thumbs-down. Failing the primary interface in a 3D video game means that the developers do not know or care about their job. So I don't care about their game. Learn your interface already, developers! It's not funny any more. Everybody looks at graphics quality, but the actual
of the 3D view doesn't matter? Is everybody crazy these days?
Since 2016-11-14 (3 days after the game was published), thanks to Matti Hietanen we now have a FOV
(with the downside that the FOV resets whenever you load a savegame). It's a DLL that you have to inject into the game, which turned out to be childishly simple: 1) Run the game and also Cheat Engine. 2) In Cheat Engine, choose the game via the button at the left top button, as per usual. Then click on the "memory view" button in the left half of the window. 3) From the new window, via the "tools" menu, select "inject DLL", choose the downloaded DLL (Unpacked from the ZIP, of course.), and confirm "Execute?" with yes. Done. A window will pop up immediately that is bound to the game as you can see in the Windows task bar where the game's icon now has two windows. You can close Cheat Engine now. [PAGEUP]/[PAGEDOWN] changes the FOV, [POS1] toggles the HUD objective locators, which is super useful and should even have been a real hotkey in the game, because sometimes you just need to take a peek at where you have to go, but most of the time, you don't want that, and traversing the menus each time is just stupid.
This does not weigh into the verdict, but you should know it. No mouse or keyboard action can skip them, and renaming the files so that the game doesn't find them makes the game freeze/crash - welcome to total beginner level development. But they can be replaced with a very short video, so I made one and uploaded it to
.
There's a lot that can be said about how to (not) do the logo videos part of a product. If you're interested in that, and in a lot of other things games still do wrong so routinely, take a look at my
Very early in the game, you actually step up to a hurt person who proceeds to give you important information and then immediately dies. The very same thing happens a few missions later in the game. ... It's ok, everybody does it, e.g. the "Missing Link" section in "Deus Ex: Human Revolution". What a tired trope :(
The voice of the Outsider was a lot better in DH1. An imho completely unnecessary change and step down.
The ending ... I won't spoil it, but by now you stopped reading this paragraph, so I can say that it does feel a bit rushed, certainly as if obvious possibilities were left unexplored because time was short and therefore just the obligatory things were done, and that's it. The game is not like that in every place, but the ending has this a bit. It doesn't hurt, but it feels less than it should feel based on the story that leads up to those moments. Another thing about the ending is that a key element is quite known to Dishonored 1 players already, so it feels like the same idea has been recycled.
I've met two mission/map design that I can't describe further because of spoilers. Let's just say that the gameplay mechanisms that are employed there are a near novelty and are well implemented, a good source for fun and exploration. Must have been mind-boggling to design those. Very engaging, mind-teasing, interesting. Not just a step up from Dishonored, but somewhere in the upper levels of gaming.
It's not like Dishonored 1 squared, but it's certainly a considerable improvement
On the one hand, it's just more of the same. If you liked DH1 and its great DLCs, which I certainly did, then you will enjoy DH2. But if you were expecting something beyond, then you will realize that it's only a boosted version but not a new evolutionary step, other than some mission/map design highlights and the fact that you can play two characters with different powers, meaning that you have a lot of replay value if you don't directly chain playthroughs to each other, cause that gets boring. You have the low/high chaos variants, the stealth vs alert variants, and finally the powers vs no powers variants. That's a lot of replay value. Just, you know, give it some downtime in between.

SteamWorld Dig possesses a unique combination of old-school progression and mastery, and the modern spelunking style of gameplay.  As you dig deeper, you overcome challenges in order to unlock new mechanics that will enable to go further and solve new problems.  It's a tight, satisfying progression structure which fits into a relatively short, but satisfying time.
Post game challenges emphasize mastery, ranking the player on the speed of completion, as well as items collected and deaths endured.  It is perhaps the most approachable game of it's kind, though gaming veterans may find it to be shallow by comparison.

Steamworld dig is accourding to most people the next "Must-have" Game on the 3ds and Steam but is it really true well let's begin with the story of the game.
WARNING: Spoiler alert!
The story is about a robot named Rusty coming to a town named Tumbleton when he falls into his uncle's mine. When he falls into the mine he runs into dorothy which after a brief conversation he goes to find his father when he finds out that his uncle died in the mine so you "borrow" his pickaxe to find out what he was up to. Then after a while he falls into the second section of the mine known as Old world a nuclear plant section. Then later you reach vectron a electronic generator underground where after mining a bit ou reach the final boss of the game known as the Voltbot who plans on taking over the world making voltbots the dominant species on the planet. After destroying the voltbot the mine collapses on you and you end up dying in the mine. Then the townspeople build a statue of Rusty and then the credits roll...ok I know what your thinking why didn't I mention the townspeople well because all they really do in the game is give you upgrades to your tools.
The Gameplay:
The gameplay is a mix of Metroid and Minecraft. But what do you do in steamworld dig you mine then sell your ore then go back to the mine then sell and so on. It doesn't sound like much but it's a really addicting game. Like Minecraft the main goal is to well Mine. Like Metroid the game is setup like a maze except you make the path But when you leave the cave it doesn't reset so you need to think out a move before you do it. But there is one major flaw it ends too soon just when your used to everything the game ends with the only boss in the game the voltbot also it takes around 5-6 hours to beat give or take. Yet this is also the best thing in the game too because when you beat the game it posts your score so it makes you destined to come back to beat your last score. Also there's another flaw  which are the side characters they just don't do anything but upgrade your tools.
The Verdict:
Steamworld dig is one of those masterpieces that comes around every once in a while where a game is so good you always remember the experience you had playing the game. This game is a must have game in anyone's steam library. The game is $9.99 and that is a great price so this game gets a 9.5 out of 10.

So Firaxis came out with their X-COM remake and it was good enough for a sequel, but it was a little simplified & dumbed down for streamlining's sake. Xenonauts started work before X-COM and it falls in a sweet spot between hedging more towards the complexity of the original, while updating the game/UI just enough to feel fresh and updated. It doesn't have nearly as huge a budget as firaxis musters, so it's 2D with relatively simple (but effective and pleasantly depressive) graphical design. But it requires more strategic depth than the flash-boom-pow Firaxis focused on; more troops, more deadly enemies and more actions per turn. It's got actually worthwhile base building, with an engaging air-combat dimension that Firaxis bailed on entirely. While the plot/characterization is done more subtly, the writing is quite good and putting an alien invasion in the middle of the cold war sets a very believable and engaging tone/plot arc that I don't think the game gets enough credit for.
***king aliens with death rays just landed, you've got a couple dudes with M-16's wearing paper mache, the chances of them making it out of this alive are VERY SLIM, and you can see it on their faces. Xenonauts sells this sense of peril MUCH better than the other Xcom reboots managed.
I really liked Firaxis' X-COM & X-COM 2. I think maaaaybe X-COM 2 edges out Xenonauts, but they had millions more budgeted to get there. Xenonauts is much more bang for your buck, and Goldhawk did fantastic job for such a little company.

Xenonauts is the true heir to the X-COM games from the mid-90s. You don't hand out equipment at the beginning of each mission, you give everyone a desired loadout from the base screen, and you can see their stats and achievements and rank all in the same screen (instead of the like, 3, from the old game)
In other words if you liked the old X-COM you will love this. Especially with the Community Edition. It is just as, if not more, challenging, and it's just as atmospheric and spooky as the old game.

The best zombie survival game ive ever played, this isnt your regular zombie game. guns arent always available and ammo is sparce. You need to be aware of everything around you and where you are. This game pushes you to the limits when it comes to teamwork. There is absolutely no way to win this if you dont work as a team. You need to defend zones or do specific tasks in order to survive the zombie apocalypse. This is probably the most realistic zombie game you will find. If you like survival games you will love this game. It a great game to kill some time and play with friends. It is also one of the hardest games ive ever played. Its going to take a while before you successfully survive or escape in a map. Once you know what you're doing though, its incredible fun.
Pros:
-You need to coordinate with your teammates. I see this more as a pro than a con, but I know some people will see it as a con when you get teammates who are just wasting ammo and dying. But being forced to work together whether its with strangers,friends, or both makes the game realistic and really give you the feeling of "i cant survive the zombie apocalypse alone, i have to work with people i may never meet in real life"
-Realistic environment
-Really requires you to think about what you are doing
-Variety of weapons
-Tons of zombies to kill :D
Cons:
-The characters have no personality. You can choose from voice sets but no personality slightly makes the game feel less realistic.
-No variety of characters. Most wont see this as a downside But all the characters are male caucasian adults besides one who is african american. No old survivors or young survivors, no females. They are working on a female character but for now this is a pretty noticable downside.
-Beginners will be turned off by long respawn times in conjunction with them dying multiple times. This comes with a lot of games but most dont have really long respawn times which is the next round, which can last up to ten more minutes if your teammates are having trouble and dont have the items to start hunting.
I definitely recommend the game even with those cons. The characters cons arent too big a problem and easy to get over and theyre very small points. In terms of long respawn times, yes incredibly frustrating but once you know what you are doing you can survive multiple rounds without dying.

So here's the deal. The game itself is pretty cool. And I recommend the game itself. Buuuuuutttt...

I have a GTX 1070, i5 4690K, and 16GB DDR3. I'd say that if you have less than a GTX 1060, RX 480, or GTX 970 you might want to give it a pass or at least be really cautious. WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW:
(Which Guilty Gear Xrd is the right one?) The most current one is Rev2, which also has the most users currently. It is an expansion of Revelator. You can get the full package by getting Rev and Rev2 for $45, or get the game with every DLC pack for $60 (you MUST buy Revelator to get Rev2. Sign is a seperate game entirely). Steam sales do not apply.
Positives:
+AMAZING 3d characters modeled to look like 2d characters.
+Fantastic Anime artstyle and hard rock soundtrack.
+25 characters, each with their own completely unique design and gameplay. I GUARANTEE your favorite character will be in this game!
+BEST TUTORIAL IN ANY FIGHTING GAME! Jack-O teaches you the basics by letting you fight her minions! LEARN AND HAVE FUN PLAYING MINIGAMES WHILE DOING IT!
+Little FAQ bubbles every time you pause will help you master the basics, among other things!
+M.O.M. mode makes for a great single player experience collecting power-ups and stat boosters to fight the cpu!
+Very smooth online experience with frame delay shown at all times!
+FANTASTIC lobby system! Create your own little avatar and walk around in rooms with up to 8 or sometimes 64 players!
+One of the most complex 2d fighting games out there with SO MUCH to learn!
Negatives:
-Confusing presentation at first. Navigating the menus and various other things will take a few tries.
-Confusing story mode (encyclopedia and other useful things help, but only for so far).
-Tutorial teaches you the bare basics of how fighting games are played, but not much detail into bursts, faultless defence, blitz shield, and all of the things that make Guilty Gear stand out from other fighting games.
-Players have fled Ranked and currently stick around in custom lobbies.
-Worth $45? $60? Probably for online mode or playing with friends, but not much else.
-Lack of GGPO (although not a big deal for most, since online is pretty smooth)
-One of the most complex 2d fighting games out there with SO MUCH to learn...
WHAT DO YOU THINK?
There's so much love put into every little detail like the presentation, the bursts, the defence, the combos however long or short, the character designs, and even little things like making a little square-headed avatar for lobbies and fishing for random cosmetics that it's really hard not to love this game if you're really into fighters. If you're not, it's going to be hard getting into Guilty Gear (especially at it's price range), but the tutorial in this game will get you on the right foot. If you like this game and need some help, now is the time to join. New players are already joining Rev2 in anticipation for Dragonball Fighters Z, ArcSys's newest title. I recommend getting this game on sale at some point, but otherwise is such a good fighter. Get some friends and join us on Discord! You won't regret it!

I jumped into this game head first. I played about 30 hours BEFORE realizing I could ADD terrain back and not just subtract it. I was enjoying it that much even with that huge disadvantage. Literal mother-effing gamechanger.
For me, a very simple man, the worlds, physics, and in-game tech are diverse enough that I can keep coming up with little personal goals to keep me occupied. Almost 60 hours in, and I've only really developed a fully-functioning base on the starting planet, and am 50-75% of the way to a similar base on another. The planets each provide unique challenges that require some strategization to approach. The terrible side of me would greatly enjoy if there were lil' native critters on each planet that I could choose to hunt to extinction just for funsies, but that's more of a pipe dream than genuine criticism.
So far, I've died from suffocation, flying debris, falls, and poison. Even being a simple man, I'm looking forward to this list of things being longer. Cave-ins, falling rocks, pools of acid (maybe?), fire (maybe?), xenomorphs (or some other un-sueable walking alien, maybe?), space madness, ghosts, radiation exposure, micrometeorites (or just storms that can damage your base, maybe?), etc etc, I'm not really complaining, as I'm sure the Astro Dev team has other stuff up their sleeve, I'm just saying to anyone who has yet to play there isn't much YET. Hi,
I've spent roughly 4 hours with Dishonored 2 tonight, and being fairly happy with my experience so far, I thought I'd log my thoughts here.
JFYI, I've just arrived in Karnaca, so I spent 3.8. hours in Dunwall and on the ship. Dishonored is a game that you need to take slowely; let its lore sink in, read all the "books" you can find, and take your time to reflect and to connect the dots. If you're an achievement-oriented gamer, this might not be the ideal game for you, but if you're interested in a meaty background story explaining the universe Dishonored 2 is based in, you'll be pleased.
Pros
-----
* Amazing art style
* Nice pacing (not too few and not too many "books" to read)
* Level design (feels organic, lots of optional areas to explore so far)
* Sound (Top notch, from voice acting to the sound of water crushing against the whaler's hull)
* Lots of freedom (you've got to choose between playing two different characters and whether to use (super) powers or not)
* Seems stable (no crashes within the first four hours)
* Love the references to the first Dishonored title.
Cons
-----
* Story opening could've been more interesting (take-over of power followed by an escape, seriously?)
Setup
------
i7-4790k (4.0 GHz)
Asus Maximus Impact VII (Mini ITX)
Asus Strix GTX 980 Ti (6 GB GDDR5)
Asus ROG SWIFT PG278Q (playing on 2560x1440)
16 GB RAM (DDR 3)
~3 TB of Samsung SSDs (EVO 840/850)

First of all i am a big fan of Dishonored 1. Second.. i am playing on a i7 6700K at 4.2 Ghz with 32 gigs of ram, ssd and a GTX1070 with everything except depth of field turned to max.
The goods:

The bad:

- The enemy AI is as clunky as the D1 at pathways.
- The audio is nothing special for me. Corvo is boring. Emily seems okay.
- Game crashed at Clockwork Mansion after the mechanical soldiers attacked me on sight right after i entered the mansion.. what a badly designed game..
I am sorry but i see no real point to recommend this game at the current price. Maybe at 19 euros.. If you want a solid stealth/action experience you can play Dishonored 1 without any tech issues.

The gameplay consists of exploring areas for slimes, abducting slimes, and farming for crops to feed your slimes, use said crops to feed your slimes, and sell the♥♥♥♥♥♥that comes out of them. It seems fun at first glance, but it gets really repetitive after a while. Not only that, but the game itself has a little amount of content for the price it's set at. Yes, it is in early access, but if you ask me, that is a♥♥♥♥♥♥excuse. Using that logic, I could publish a game that looks good, but only has 1 hour of content for $30. Sure, I could add more content, but you won't be guaranteed that nor will you know when the exact date that it becomes a finished product. I'll give the creators credit for creating luscious areas to explore along with the cute slimes they created, but regardless, they really shouldn't have priced this game at $20. The most you're going to get is about 2-4 hours of content, and that's if you're enjoying the game and not abducting all the slimes to profit out of them. You might be thinking "but they're going to add more content, right?". They most likely will, they aren't Code}{atch. That is a bit reassuring,
, even though they're working hard on this game, you're not going to get much from future updates. Alongside that, their small team is going to take a long time to accomplish all the things that the roadmap has to offer. It took them almost 2 years (excluding the recent update) to make this much content. That is impressive for a small team, but that doesn't mean that you should release a game with this much content at a price of $20. They could've either spent more time to add more content to this game and then release it, as opposed to releasing this game now and lowering several people's expectations. If you ask me, don't buy this game if you aren't too sure on buying this game, use that money on some other game. However, if you REALLY want the game, then by all means buy it, don't let my opinion discourage you from buying the game if you really want it.

Some of the alien races were cool.
Soldiers are more personalized, because they have names, but also nationality and service history; for example Russian soldiers could be veterans of Afghanistan, etc..
The entire late 70's ambience was neat and there were several other features to capitalize on it, like UFO bombing various civilian or military targets (passenger liners, carriers etc.), not just city terrors.
Nevertheless, this game sadly had a number of problems that make it inferior to the X-Com franchise.
The gameplay wasn't as exciting as I hoped.
Battles were slow, aliens were tough, there was a lot of stalling and just laying cover fire across the street, because it was very hard to kill even the weakest alien with normal weapons.
I found it rather boring and a bit frustrating at times.
Next some parts of maps (mainly UFOs) were indestructible. To me, this was unpleasant and hurt the immersion. It was so because the ships were painted in whole, and they looked nice, but I'd trade it any moment for destructible UFO walls. Open X-COM, baby.

Pros:
• Has the 'fun' factor. I have spent too many hours playing WC3 Warlocks and am a big fan of that game. I have also played other Warlocks inspired games, like Spellsworn and RUiN, and this game captures the 'fun' factor the best out of all of them. I feel like you can put many hours in this game, and every round will feel unique and exciting.
• Beautiful art and graphics. I love the arcade theme, and the abundance of arenas to choose from. The projectile particles look great too.
• 100% individual skill based. I love that I don't have to rely on teammates to do their part. I can only blame myself if I lost :).
• Lots of spells and a good variety of different robots to play with.
Cons:
• Lack of players.
• Region-locked. I can understand it if the game has an enormous player base, but that's not the case here. I'm willing to compromise on the latency if that means I can get a game going when I want to play.
• Physics system is somewhat clunky. It looks like there's a noticeable delay between a projectile hitting you and the knockback occurring. Also, I put up a reflective barrier, and things that should have been reflected were just passing through the barrier.
Small suggestions for the devs:
• Too much downtime between rounds. There is currently a full minute between rounds, which is only spent by picking spells. I suggest allowing "practice" spell shooting and movement during this time (this is what Warlocks does).
• Hotkeys are different after each game. When you pick a spell, it just goes to the next slot in the ability bar. I suggest creating a menu that allows the player to bind all spells to certain hotkeys (per robot).
Conclusion:
It's an early access game, and with early access comes bugs and issues (no developer can escape this). If you have played WC3 Warlocks before, or have played some type of arena brawler and love those kinds of games, then I feel like at $12.99 you will be getting a good bang for your buck. Please keep in mind that at this point, it is difficult to get a game going because of the lack of players and the region locking (join the Discord server to help with this). I feel like there's a lot of potential here, and I am looking forward to destroying lots of robots and watching the community grow :).
Note: I will try to update this review as the game gets updated.

SteamWorld Dig is a really clever and unique 2d platformer. Sort of a Minecraft meets Metroidvania. With steampunk robots in a Wild West setting. I don't remember why I grabbed this one. But I'm really glad I did.
You play as a robot who's uncle has sent for you to come to his mine in the town he lives in. When you get there, you fall into a hole and meet a girl-robot in the mine who shows you to your uncle's dead (deactivated?) corpse (or junk pile, not sure if robots have a corpse). Well now, you own the mine and your uncles mining pick. Welcome to Steamworld, population of 3.
So the basic thing is, you have a pick. You go down into the mine and mine around, looking for ore to take back to the surface and sell. Every x dollars worth of ore you bring up, you get the option to buy an upgrade from the nearby shop. There are many different types of ore you bring up, all worth differing amounts. There are also various enemies, trapped in the rock or running in tiny caverns. You can stay in the mine as long as you want, but you do have a light that slowly runs out, causing the illumination to get dimmer and dimmer until it evertually is gone. When this happens, you can barely see and definately cant see the ore you are looking for. Upgrades are things like stronger picks, longer light, stronger armor, more inventory slots and so on. There are also ladders and lamps, which can be purchased for cheap and placed in the mine but not picked up again, once they're there, they're there.  You can carry up to 4 lamps and 5 ladders, (in the beginning anyway), but wasting them sucks even though they are cheap.
There is also a little story, and various caves "your uncle hid stuff in". The caves have cool power ups, things like an extra high "steam jump", the ability to sprint and other permanent power ups. Just like Metroidvania style games, getting these power ups allows you to access areas that were blocked to you before.
The graphics are cute and slightly cartoony, but very well done. Each character (besides you) has a portrait when you talk to them, and all sprites and images are rendered well in vibrant color.
The music is Western sounding and fits the scenery well. Other sounds are typical as expected for mining in a steampunk world inhabited by robots (pings, clanks, stones falling, steam hissing) but all are appropriate and not intrusive. One important sound is the popping noise an enemy imprisoned in the rock makes as it tries to break out. Killing these enemies while still imprisoned is important, as they can be killed in one hit, but if they break free (by having open space near them, they become harder to kill and harm you if you hit them).
The controls arent quite as perfect as some platformers Ive played (Dust and Thomas Walks Alone come to mind as two platformers with near perfect controls) but they arent terrible. You wont be missing jumps due to poor controls and getting frustrated, but neither they arent that perfect almagam that makes the character feel like an extention of the controller.
You can't mine while jumping or wall jumping- a way to go up a shaft by bouncing along the walls). Also you cant mine (at least at the point I'm at, dont know if an upgrade changes that) other than the block directly above you without a ladder. So if you want something above you and dont want to waste ladders, you must go all the way back up and mine from on top of it to get it. Thats kind of annoying in my mind.
Also, if you accidentally drop a ladder in a one-square high tunnel, you cant mine directly above or below it while standing on the same sqaure as the ladder. That is REALLY annoying, and something I think the devs should fix.
Overall, this game is quite fun as you mine deeper and deeper in search of treasure, creating strange tunnels nad paths as you go. It does have a self-destruct feature in case you pin yourself due to falling rocks or bad judgement, but pinning yourself is not a common occurance. Death takes half your money, which seems kind of steep as the minerals do not appear to regenerate at all. But dying is rather rare, as easy to kill trapped enemies which drop recovery items are abundant.

Really, stay away for now. Needs more time in the oven. Too many issues here that stretch from some of the weirdest♥♥♥♥♥♥I've ever seen in a game to the standard severe FPS drops and random stuttering.
Sensitivity is all kinds of ♥♥♥♥ed up. Literally. Certain parts of the game will see your sensitivity shoot up to max sensitivity where others will lower it to single digits for no reason at all. It doesn't seem to be tied to your FPS either which is weird. It's literally just tied to whatever area you're looking at(Higher FPS = lower sensitivity while lower FPS = higher sensitivity). This is with smoothing off and VSync off. Turning VSync on masks the issue a bit but it's still bloody noticable. In the opening gameplay area if you look out to the ocean you'll get lower FPS but MUCH higher mouse sensitivity yet looking at a wall and getting much higher FPS you get much LOWER mouse sensitivity. I've never experienced anything quite like it in my gaming years. I've had games where FPS was tied to VSync and games where it was tied to FPS(Where lower FPS = lower sensitivity and higher = higher sensitivity) but never anything like this. This is just... Holy crap how could they release the game like this?!
Then there's the performance issues(Which PCGamer have written an article about -- it's not pretty boys and girls...). My god the performance issues. My first combat area I went, for absolutely no reason, from 80FPS to 25FPS and the FPS was stuck around the 25-33FPS mark for the entire area. Completely unplayable. Not only is it low FPS but very high and inconsistent frame times(Which translates to stutter or micro stutter). It's really, really bad... The forums are alight with people complaining on all kinds of set ups(i7-6700k's, GTX 1080's, 1070's, RX 480's, R9 390's). It's really bad and pretty much unplayable as is.
My first impression after an hour of playing is just sheer disappointment. The story starts off badly and makes NO sense from a logical standpoint(Spoiler, Deliah just walks in and claims she's the real Empress and everyone just turns on Corvo and Emily who then immediately go on a killing spree... all of this happened "just because."). It's such a bad start...
The controls are also pretty ♥♥♥♥ing dumb in parts. I mean, it's a stealth game, it's not an action FPS game... so why do we have a slide ability that's tied to your "stealth" key? lol? You can't even rebind the key. Slide makes more noise and alerts everyone around to your presence so why on earth is the key to use it also your ♥♥♥♥ing stealth key?! It's. So. Dumb.
Honestly, wait on this. Do yourself a favour and wait. I was really excited for this, it was going to be my GOTY(I had my heart set on it!) but this is a really poor showing. Either it's a♥♥♥♥♥♥poor PC port or the game really needed to be left in development for a few months more to polish it, we'll have to hear what it's like on consoles to really deduce which it is.
Also, the graphics aren't great. The AA options are terrible and do next to nothing to remove jaggies(It's only post processing AA... Like, did you even try, Arkane?)... I'm so disappointed.

BIAS NOTE: I personally think the Original X-Com / UFO is the best game ever made, so my opinion is slightly loaded.
Xenonauts is an old school base management and turn based tactical strategy game based on the 1993 game X-Com: UFO defence / UFO: Enemy Unknown designed to savagely punish and bemuse the unwary, but inside many rewarding things can be found.
If there has been one marker of the 2010s in games it has been nostalgia goggles. In the late 2000s the mid 20 to 40 something have been looking back on the games they grew up on and wonder why the IPs are being abused and how the content they grew up on now no longer exists. Weird reboots of series such as Syndicate and the announced X-Com sat badly with people and much yelling happened. Then Kickstarter happened, and... the less said about Kickstarter as a whole the better. Some results however were fantastic and Goldhawk Interactive's Xenonauts was a good example of a dev sticking to the original quite tightly.
For old X-Com / UFO players Xenonauhts is a very faithful update to the original series containing the iconic tactical map, intercepting, base management and, of course, the turn based ground missions. The whole game will no doubt be extremely familiar to old X-Com vets and within a few minutes you will be back to reserving Time Units for snap shots and figuring out how to research those alien corpses.
Xenonauts does make some small updates and the game is different in subtle ways, mainly in the context of balance, streamlining and user friendliness. Air combat is more interesting with areal dogfights being a bit more interactive, ground combat involves less clicking about and a number of fluffy items have been removed e.g. mind probes and while there are the clear super-powered weapons, there are no blaster launchers with an almost magical "I win" button effect. The interface and micromanagement has also been overhauled, for example ammo management, manufacture, purchase and scavenging is not as much of a stress as the original games, but at the same time the big money makers like selling the excess enemy weapons and corpses are done away with. Essentially you are not going to play database sim while trying to figure out what you have and have not researched.
While the game has clearly been rebalanced around these new systems, it is still the same as the original in the context of how bloody minded and unforgiving it is. Unless you save-scum (which Ironman mode helps you resist) early missions are more than likely going to be bogged down with many, many dead soldiers. Even on easy mode this game is brutally unforgiving and will quite happily kill your commander with a reaper from behind.
Reapers in this game are essentially Chryssalids. Yeah, they brought them back.
A major turn off for many however will be the abstract nature of the game. Like the new reboot of Xcom Xenonauts also includes the diceroll random luck when you attack enemies. One second you will get a perfect crit damage shot from a human pistol miles from the target and take down a Andron in one hit, then you use the Mag carbine (basically the top end shotgun that fires railgun slugs) at point blank range and somehow miss with all the every pellet. While you can indeed be very tactical and be a military genius in reality, in game you will sometimes just come out unlucky as the guy with the LMG gets mind controlled sitting a few feet away from the remainder of your crew. Ultimately this is one of the strongest pulls the X-Com series always had so it would be rather unfaithful to remove it, but if you absolutely want a game of skill without any behind the scenes dice-rolling abstraction then this game is not advised at all.
At the end of the day Xenonauts is either a love letter to the old fans, or if new a masochistic punch in the face. If you are looking for a turn based strategy game that will punish you, regardless of if you deserve it or not at times, then this one is a good pick.
And yes they brought back Cryssalids. THEY BROUGHT BACK THE MOST FRIGGING EVIL MOSTER IN GAMING HISTORY! WHY GOD?! OH WHY?!?!?!?

Xenonauts is basically a faithful remake of the original classic Xcom (not the recent new Xcom remake by Firaxis). Now if you played and loved the classic Xcom, you will definitely love Xenonauts as it plays almost identically like the classic (with some improvements). If you've only played (and loved) the Xcom remake, then be warned, Xenonauts plays very differently. I personally found the Xcom:EU remake annoying but loved Xenonauts, so i imagine those that loved Xcom:EU might find Xenonauts frustrating.
If you've never played any Xcom before, then the game is probably only recommended for those who love a 'hardcore' turn-based squad-level strategy game. The game has a base-building resource management strategic layer, but the real meat of the game is in the tactical combat. You will be spending hours fighting battle after battle, poring over each squaddie's movement and facing, trying to flank enemies, agonizing over decisions to rush troops in the line of enemy fire, or taking risky shots with allies in the field of fire etc. If you don't enjoy tactical squad combat, then you won't enjoy this game. Take note, you WILL lose soldiers, don't get too frustrated over that.
I completed the game on normal mode. Had to reload the game a few times due to some stupid tactical errors, but i didn't find anything to be too unfair/punishing. I don't play ironman on the first run-through cause i want to make sure i can reach the ending and i don't want to waste time constantly restarting. The game can get a bit repetitive  and 'grindy' in the later stages but taking my high leveled elite squad to the final battle and practically breezing through with almost my entire squad surviving and escaping was pretty satisfying.
The only cons i have (other than slightly grindy later stages) would be the boring air combat system. After a few rounds of air combat, i resorted to just using auto resolve as i didn't find the air combat particularly engaging.
Overall i enjoyed the game. I especially loved some of the improvements over the classic Xcom:
- More organized squad equip/management with ability to customize your own soldier roles/class
- A handy line of fire indicator so i know what objects are in the way
- A nice suppression fire system (suppressed units cannot take reaction shots and start with only half TU's on their turn)
- No more hunting the last alien hiding in some basement somewhere. Mission ends if you clear the UFO of all enemies for 5 turns.
- if you are bored of sending your troops on ground missions, just airstrike UFO's from the air for some cash.

Bought this game a while ago and thought it was time to write a review.
If you love the old UFO/XCOM games (the MSDOS ones from Microsoft) you will love this game.
It is VERY similar comapred to those classics, with of course imrpoved graphics and gameplay.
Everything you loved in the old games is here..and more....or better,sometimes both.
The intercepting of an ufo for example. Now you can control andgive directions to your fighters,where to fly,to evade,afterburner etc. Its possible to shoot down a large UFO, by using inferiour/outdated crafts and weapons, by just apllying a good strategy. Some UFOS have escort crafts, some ufos need rockets(torpedos) to make them land. There are alot of options.
The actual isometric ground combat is much harder than in the old Xcoms. The aliens are more deadly and smarter than the Mircoprose ones. It requires care and patience to surivive the first missions without casualties.
In general, the learning curve for thsi game is steeper in every aspect. The financial part is very challening. To keep your bases running and build new fighters and weapons or armor is costly. Even the base locations took me several starts to really get a cost efficient coverage of the globe.
Of course all the other game aspects from the classics are here. Base construction, research, building items, improving your squad etc are all here...but as i mentiond just better polished.
I played the early 2000 UFO games,which were realtime and hated them. I played the 2k Xcom and never really liked it. It looks flashy, but the gameplay is just boring and stale. It does not feel grand and very limited.
Xenonauts gives me all the freedom i want ...and it makes me pay for it, if i make poor decisions....but i love it.

I'm playing the community edition, which polishes up some of the mechanics.  This game is pretty solid, and well thought out.  The geoscape and air combat feel pretty authentic, and that alone sets this apart from the new XCOM.  The ground combat is tedious, but in a good way.  I'm constantly counting my TUs trying to decide when to run up to an alien to blast their face off with a shotgun, and when I pull it off, it is extremely satisfying.
The CE maps are challenging even in the early game, and this game doesn't ease you into the mechanics as much as XCOM did.  I play this game on normal difficulty, and I'm not ashamed to save scum because sometimes I still take dead soldiers at the end of a mission if the trade off was worth it.  That's because the risks and rewards in this game are balanced, and the progression is logical.  I'd reccomend this game if you like spending an hour planning every 5 minutes of action.

Sensitivity is all kinds of ♥♥♥♥ed up. Literally. Certain parts of the game will see your sensitivity shoot up to max sensitivity where others will lower it to single digits for no reason at all. It doesn't seem to be tied to your FPS either which is weird. It's literally just tied to whatever area you're looking at(Higher FPS = lower sensitivity while lower FPS = higher sensitivity). This is with smoothing off and VSync off. Turning VSync on masks the issue a bit but it's still bloody noticable. In the opening gameplay area if you look out to the ocean you'll get lower FPS but MUCH higher mouse sensitivity yet looking at a wall and getting much higher FPS you get much LOWER mouse sensitivity. I've never experienced anything quite like it in my gaming years. I've had games where FPS was tied to VSync and games where it was tied to FPS(Where lower FPS = lower sensitivity and higher = higher sensitivity) but never anything like this. This is just... Holy crap how could they release the game like this?!
Then there's the performance issues(Which PCGamer have written an article about -- it's not pretty boys and girls...). My god the performance issues. My first combat area I went, for absolutely no reason, from 80FPS to 25FPS and the FPS was stuck around the 25-33FPS mark for the entire area. Completely unplayable. Not only is it low FPS but very high and inconsistent frame times(Which translates to stutter or micro stutter). It's really, really bad... The forums are alight with people complaining on all kinds of set ups(i7-6700k's, GTX 1080's, 1070's, RX 480's, R9 390's). It's really bad and pretty much unplayable as is.

You can't even rebind the key. Slide makes more noise and alerts everyone around to your presence so why on earth is the key to use it also your ♥♥♥♥ing stealth key?! It's. So. Dumb.
Honestly, wait on this. Do yourself a favour and wait. I was really excited for this, it was going to be my GOTY(I had my heart set on it!) but this is a really poor showing. Either it's a♥♥♥♥♥♥poor PC port or the game really needed to be left in development for a few months more to polish it, we'll have to hear what it's like on consoles to really deduce which it is.
Also, the graphics aren't great. The AA options are terrible and do next to nothing to remove jaggies(It's only post processing AA... Like, did you even try, Arkane?)... I'm so disappointed.

Slime Rancher is a fun, cute game where you capture jiggly, bouncy little slime creatures on an alien planet, corral them up, and feed them so you can harvest their♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ which is a very valuable resource in whatever space-future the game takes place in.
The economy is literally♥♥♥♥♥♥♥
It's similar to games like Harvest Moon or Minecraft, where you don't really have any definite end goal, and just farm resources, expand your ranch, and upkeep everything indefinitely.
It's good for people that like micromanaging everything; I find myself almost constantly running around between all of my slimes' enclosures, because there's always something that needs doing.
One of the bigger draws of the game, I feel, is the player's ability to combine different types of slimes by feeding them other slimes' Plorts. It actually makes me think of Tamagotchi; you want to keep playing to see what kinds of slimes you can create. There are a lot of different types of slimes, and they each have their own characteristics, so you have to think about what traits you want when combining slimes, as well as the value of the Plorts they produce.
Some only eat fruit, but if you combine them with one that eats vegetables, they can eat both.
Some slimes are more docile and tame, and easier to manage, while others are GIANT JERKFACES.
I'M TALKING TO YOU, ROCK SLIMES, YOU RUDE, ROLLING BALLS OF BLUE♥♥♥♥♥♥♥

I haven't really encountered many bugs in my time playing, and those I did were pretty small. Nothing game-breaking by any means, just minor inconveniences.
The game doesn't have a ton of content at the moment, but there seems to be a lot more coming later, and what's here will still provide plenty to do. Unfortunately, I can't promise you'll feel it's worth $20; once you look past the cute exterior, the actual gameplay is pretty simplistic, and it won't take you too long to do everything the game has to offer.
I still recommend it, though, because it's the type of game you can easily find yourself playing for hours and hours, well after you've exhausted everything there is to do thrice over.
Plus, it's really cute.

At the moment I cannot give this game a favorable review.  I've supported Trek and Mr. Prassel in their previous attempts such as Orion: Prelude and such and even bought this game when it came out as Guardians of Orion.  The game was, at the start, littered with bugs rendering it unplayable for many people.  I stopped playing the game early on after Prassel got annoyed with some of the bug reports and basically said the problems were the users' faults and not his (that he basically wasn't going to spend time fixing the issue since it only affected a small portion of the community).  I came back months later after new updates to see if any of the issues were resolved.  Sadly, the game still has a million and one technical issues (including poor optimization for many PCs).  INSTEAD of fixing the issues, Trek and Prassel are pushing new content rather than addressing problems.  A few members of the community have even narrowed down certain problems so that any fix would be easier to spot but there has been no response from the development team whether on the forums or in email.
Technical issues can be fixed but the lack of response and childish behavior from the development team push this game into a "thumbs down" for the time being.  If things change I might possibly revert that.
***********
Original Edit Following:  Mr. Prassel's comment regarding specificity to this review shall be obliged below.  I'll try to be as concise as possible.
***********
First, regarding technical support.  While I realize that it makes technical support's job easier to know everyone's tech specs, this is almost impossible when a forum is created asking for bug reports (even if it specifies that those specs are needed).  When a person comes to the team with a problem, regardless of how aggravated the team may be, respond simply and with a "copy/pasted" answer such as, "Please submit your technical specifications and we'll review your issue."  Do not just ignore people; that applies to both forum posts and any emails received.  In fact, in a post from Dec 16th, 2015 Mr. Prassel stated anyone could contact him with this [a problem in that thread] or any problem at: [won't post the email here].  I and a few others have personally sent emails to Trek and Mr. Prassel but received no response.  Perhaps the emails have been overlooked, sent to spam, etc...  These things happen and I will acknowledge that is a possibility.
Second, the following threads show various issues that have been fixed and not been fixed to demonstrate that people in this community do care and try to help with the development while providing the necessary details. A game in which I would let my 13 week old baby play. Does not have the feel like it is going to expand upon itself. Pretty basic and can be boring within the first hour. If a game doesn't catch you within that time. Why play it? I get if you live with your parents and can play games nonstop, but for someone with a 40+ work week looking for a game to relax and enjoy, THIS IS NOT IT.

So far, I am really enjoying Astroneer. In my two first "worlds" or "universes", I was unsuccessful in learning how to play the game. I hadn't watched gameplay prior to playing the game myself (save the trailer), and I felt somewhat lost. Feeling frusterated, I didn't play the game for a couple of weeks. Eventually, I decided to give it another try, and this time, I was able to follow the beginning "tutorial" much more successfully and locate the necessary resources. In the case that other players are stuck like I was, I reccommend going caving and salvaging valuable resources out of other abandoned spacecraft, because often times they contain necessary items to continue to expand your base. Since then, I have been able to experiment with what seems to be a 3-D printing dock, and I was overjoyed to discover that I had the resources to craft a rover, which I did promptly of course. I definitely reccommend buying this game while it's still in early access, because I truly believe it has the potential to become mainstream in the future, or should I say... mainSTEAM.

Better than the original XCOM? Yes - much less micromanagement, improved air combat & UI
Better than the recent XCOM reboot? Yes - ground combat much closer to the original (more realistic focus on cover and visibility), overall it feels less scripted and linear
So, the definitive version of one of the best strategy games ever made then? Yes!
For those unfamiliar with the original XCOM, it's a fairly standard base management game punctuated by possibly the most tense, terrifying turn-based squad elements you'll ever play. It's arguably the greatest game created by two giants of the computer game industry, Julian Gollop & Sid Meier.
The only slight criticism for me is that I preferred the droney music of the original which increased the atmosphere. Also, I'm pretty sure they've (rather naughtily) lifted sections of Ennio Morricone's score for The Thing!
I also recommend downloading the free Community Edition update for more maps and improved UI.

Xenonauts suffers from what many other games of this type suffer from, and that is "click to roll dice.  input not required further.  listed results not guaranteed, unless it disadvantages player".  This is probably the best game in this genre in many years, far surpassing the Xcom remakes, but is still more of a dice simulator than a game.  Actual gameplay does exist in Xenonauts, but its built in such a way that every decision is a pass/fail state.  IE, build your starting base in the wrong place, fail after an hour or two.  Build in the right place, survive for a couple hours.  Research the right techs and build the right corresponding devices, extend playtime 30 minutes to an hour.  Build anything else, end gameplay with failstate.  This will continue until the game over screen or the campaign victory screen.  Its a lot like hardcore 2d platformers in that its all about memorizing the right steps to take at the right times.
The most painful aspect to this is that you can easily survive awhile with the wrong decision, which gives you a false sense of progress, only to run into a brick wall that jolts you with "hmmm so choosing X tech over Y tech an hour ago would have trivialized this new threat/mechanic."  That is all there is to this game. Positioning of your soldiers in ground combat is nearly exactly the same.  There are 2 or 3 tactics that are nearly guaranteed to win you battles, and about a million tactics that literally wipe out your entire squad/fleet/base in a single round and end your campaign, and most succesful tactics involve exploiting some factor of the design.  Save scumming is easy in this game but really isnt that useful unless you want to avoid the dozens of hours required to get to the next pass/fail state and figure out the required move(hint: save scum for awhile to figure it out, then play a perfect campaign at whatever difficulty you want.  then uninstall. otherwise your just going to end up disapointed with the time you spent running the campaign to figure out the states).
Something about the artwork and written lore however, really give this game VASTLY more atmosphere and character than the high budget cutscene and voice acting laden sexed up Xcom remakes.  That is both a compliment to Xenonauts and a slash on the Xcoms, but the fact remains there is almost nothing redeeming about this style of game. Getting attached to your soldiers is something much talked about, but neither Xcom nor xenonauts really have any personality in the characters and thus losing them is really only troubling due to losing a unit that has higher on screen dice rolls that ultimately are utterly meaningless given the inherent hit/death gameplay.  Much has also been made about the difficulty and Ironman modes, and to that i refer you to the wall of text i just wrote.
If you are into it though, then Xenonauts is the best game you can buy in this genre on the market currently in my opinion.  It at least feels the most like a game and seems to be from developers that are genuinely interested in fake gameplay and interesting universes.

This game is a pretty standard example of how to milk a game for all it is worth using already existing assets.
I was an original player from back when the game was owned and run by Real Time Worlds (R.I.P) and published by EA. I was one of the first batch of players to play APB Reloaded during the closed beta period. After open beta is began it's continuous downward spiral.
Pros
- Customization, it's nearly unmatched in the options for customizations
Cons
- Poor community and lack of in-game moderating; griefers, hackers and inappropriate behavior that isn't punished.
- Dominated by in-game microtransaction system; you'll rarely find people that play consistently who don't spend money in some form. It's not impossible to play without paying, takes a noticeable amount of time for it to be worth it.
- Unoptimized.
- Poor matchmaking; back during closed beta there weren't districts that were divided by 'threat level', so often times higher ranked players would get matched against many more people than were in their group. I consider that a step up to what is currently in the game.
- Poor spawn system; pretty easy to push on a spawn so the enemy spawns farther away, and car spawners have completely ruined the dynamic of the game.

Figured I might as well write a review because this game obviously needs more positive reviews!
To get right into it:
Pros:
-A whole LOT of content even without the DLCs. (but they're each so much fun you might as well get them too!)
-Every character has their own backstory and unique personality. Whether Player character or NPC (In the Psycho's case he has two.)
-Each playable character has 3 skill trees so even you two people play the same character they  can still play them differently.
-The experience gain is paced really well so that by the end of the game you should complete your first skill tree and then be ready for your next one when you start the next difficulty.
-The next difficulty ACTUALLY PLAYS DIFFERENTLY than the last! You run into more elite (Badass) enemies and elemental advantages/disadvantages are Much more Apparent. They don't just crank up the numbers and call it more content!
-Handsome Jack is a villian you will LOVE to HATE! He's simultaneuosly hilarious, narcicssistic, and evil as all hell!
-Each side quest is it's own little story. Whether you're covering for an injured delivery boy or collecting friends for a tea party you're never sent on a mission without a clear reason why and some often times hilarious dialogue to go with it.
-Voice acting isreally good! No complaints in that department.
-This game is pretty old so when it goes on sale the sales are Hella On Sale!
-4 PLAYER CO-OP.
Cons:
-It's not uncommon for dialogue/subtitles to run over each other when certain events take place at the same time.
-This is a more artistic gnit pick, but Gearbox could use some work when it comes to acting animation.
-Looting can get a little stale after a while. I often run into long patches of loot I don't really need (Kind of dealt with in True Vault Hunter Mode (Hard mode) when I need more elemental guns)

Due the text-limit here, I wasn't able to go super-in-depth with my "review".
However, if you are interested of more of the details, here is a link to the (semi-WIP) document I wrote:
---
---
---
(( Fore-note: I've yet to play any commercial “Xcom-clones” (E.G. “UFO - Extraterrestials”) or many of the more or less open-source or freeware-projects (E.G. “Xenowar” or “UFO: Alien Invasion”.
So my “review” sticks strictly to “(Open)Xcom”-project. ))
((( First playthrough was played in “Community Edition 0.34.2”-version alongside few other tweaks. )))
---
“Xenonauts” in a summary is a streamlined and more simple but otherwise quite “1:1”-version of (Open)Xcom.
While this is a commercial-product, I personally consider this game to be more of experimental-project to create a good and faithful "clone-game".
This is an opinion formed especially reading through the "Development Diary"-entries found all around places (E.G. "on-progress"-entries on their forums and "closure" as a PDF-file as an extra-content).
---
Here is also a comparison of Xenonauts to (Open)Xcom in “what do you get out of the package”-style.:
What do you get:
- Simplified base-management
- Reduced amount micromanaging inventory-wise
- More guaranteed soldier training
- Cover-system
- Vaulting
- More alien mission variants and events
- More control over air-combat
- More weapon & equipment type-variants
- Surprisingly good hard-science-fiction-story
- More personalities among the aliens
- Story-alerts and auto-progression
- Grenade Quick-slot
What you won’t get:
- Charts / Graphs
- Same amount ground-combat actions
- Fidelity-options
- Less tweaking possibilities
- No elevated grounds
- More complex super-weapons
- Well-enough in-depth instruction-booklet / manual
The bad(dies):
- Lots of line-of-sight bugs
- Cheating Alien Intelligence
- The almost identical “waiting-game”-problem
- “Roofed” Funding amount
- Only affected by interceptions and not ground-combat-results
- No “industrialist”-option
- Unavoidable non-Xenonaut-casulties
- Some other general bugs, especially the ones related to roof of buildings
Other mention-worthy things:
- Dropships don’t have cargo-space /weight-limit but max-personnel-amount-limit
- “Smoke-grenades” work as a significant accuracy-penalty instead of line-of-sight-reducing-block-wall-thing
- Psionics come in more variations, but can also be completely disabled (via “modding”)
- “Stun / Unconsciousness” is permanent
- You can capture / recover UFOs by clearing and holding them for five turns, thus not needing to hunt down the last strayed alien
- Modding in general
Mods come in all forms:
From simple XML-file-modifications (which pretty much anyone can do since the XML-files are “written” for the most part in plain-English, provided one knows the small “nuances” (E.G. “Time-Units” are called “ActionPoints / AP” in the XML-files)).
To more complex graphical and mechanical overhauls and additions, which also includes more-or-less total-conversions (E.G. “X-Division”).
In this regard tweaking the game for ones likings, this can be surprisingly simple:
For example I “disabled” “Hallucination”-psionic-attack by simply changing few numbers of the time-unit / action-point-cost for this particular attack-type into over the maximum value anything in this game can have in total;
I did this due how utterly un-fair it was in comparison to actual “MInd Control” (mainly because because “Berserks” happen instantly when the human / Xenonauts-turn starts (Hallucination 100%-guaranteeing them shooting at team-mates), while mind controlled-units are unavailable for two-turns and only act during alien-turns (thus allowing you to subdue the units either knocking them out or suppressing them, or simply taking cover from up-coming friendly-fire).)
I personally recommend doing most of small-tweaks (E.G. adjustments of the “Field-of-View-cone(s)) by own hand to avoid conflicts or otherwise game breaking down (especially since a large amount of the “Steam Workshop”-items are very outdated).
“Community Edition” or at least using various “Fix Packs” and such is my suggested way of playing this game, especially since they’re still on-going (as of posting this review that is).

This is both the best and worst game I have played.
But the disadvantages definitely outweigh the advantages.
First off, you join APB and it seems pretty damn cool - the customization is extremely enticing, and is probably the best thing about the whole damn game. But then after you first create your character and have gone through basic game mechanics in the tutorial, you have to begin doing "missions" which are a total and utter waste of time since the hierarchy system is as much use as a chocolate fireguard. You work through some crappy "Threat level" system ... Green, Bronze, Silver, Gold - sounds like it is fairly simple but it's not. As soon as you move from newbie Green, and into Bronze you suffer from the worst insults ever from the community just based on the bloody colour of the logo next to your name - not even on your play ability!. For anyone new, this gets bloody annoying and will surely steer people away from the game.
I have been playing this for a year now, and have been Silver only a handful of times - only to move back into Bronze. I wouldn't mind, if the matchmaking system actually worked. Now tell me GamersFirst - how is it so that 4 bronze competitors can match in skill and experience against 1 Gold and 3 Silvers for example, that have Rocket and Grenade Launchers... how are these advanced  players even able to pick that they want to be in a Bronze server? Of course when there is the "easier" option, people will take it. Therefore why not remove that opportunity and keep Golds in Gold servers and Silvers in Silver servers. This is how the game was meant to be - so why not fix it? I understand people will say "Oh there's no excuse to new people and bronzes, teamwork and skill can overcome any opponent - " No, you're having a laugh. More experienced players have more advanced mods and weapons (and sometimes even hacks, but that's only on occasion now) not to mention experience, so of course the newer players and lower down players have no chance at all.
Another thing to point out, is that most of the community has gone to shreds. Today, I was called "noob" followed by other eye-rolling names by a Silver on a Bronze server for killing them. Hmm hang on there? Killing them - that's the point of the game isn't it? And if anyone wishes to call me a "noob" so be it but - really, they're a bit of a hypocrite if they're more advanced and have to stick to the server for Bronzes and newcomers. Furthermore, people often get annoyed with newbies Team Killing them - yes so do I, but if you communicate with them and tell them that you're on their team, and help them learn instead of just expecting them to be advanced and instantly know what the hell they're doing - the APB community will become a better place, and will save any frustration.
So here's the good stuff listed:
1 Extremely addictive
2 Customization
3 Variety of weapons/mods to unlock (without having to pay with REAL MONEY on Armas Marketplace)
4 (Team Work) - [In brackets because it's not always there]
5 Rewarding missions and Fight Club is great
6 Numerous different contacts to level up
7 Season events (Halloween, Christmas etc.)
And a summary of the bad stuff:
1 Newcomers will probably find it overwhelming
2 Bronze servers littered with higher threat levels
3 Needs a new matchmaking system
4 Community needs to be more helpful and more willing to accept new players
5 More communication between players
6 Server lags often occur, especially during Fight Club due to amount of players
7 Frustration when people are "Away From Keyboard" during a mission - why not just kick them?
8 Occasional hackers
9 Just rude players genuinely ruining a game with so much potential
Ultimately, I'd say if you haven't, give this game a try. But in all honestly, it's just not worth the brain melting frustration.

However you'll find some sort of cheater in any F2P game, whether it be an aimbot, they're abusing a glitch, wallhacks, invincibility, etc. I understand that with FairFight they're trying to push back the amount of hackers in the game, but with each new day that passes by, these people will find a way to try and bypass it and survive on this game a little longer, even if it means one extra hour of tormenting the playerbase, and once that character is banned, it's that easy for them to make a whole new account and start it all over again.
However I've put up with my fair share of hackers and all that crap over the past 5 years in this game, and while it does tend to annoy me, it's never gotten to me to the point I've uninstalled APB. I just put up with it and wait for the next mission. My problem with this game at the moment, is the lack of content recently. It's been over 2 years now since the last contacts were released, and basically everyone who is R255 either sits in social cause there's nothing to do, they make a brand new character and level that to 255, rinse-repeat, or just leave the game until something new comes up to bring them back for a short period. Some players have even asked for a new game-mode, such as turf wars or racing district, instead of picking between repeated missions with the same opp, or fight club.
But what do we get instead? Joker box after joker box with a new gun that tends to be useless compared to some of the original weapons, and then you decide to release another version of that JMB weapon for credits or by forcing your players to spend 100's of dollars just to get it as a loyalty reward. I get it, a free-to-play game needs to get it's revenue from somewhere, and for APB it's the marketplace, but to care more about another gamble box over actual content for players in action districts like a new contact? No wonder why everytime I get on the game looks dead as f**k.
It really dissapoints me, as I saw alot of potential in this game, but to see where it's landed itself now makes me wish I could pull the plug on it before it suffers any longer. So to anyone who's thinking about installing this game, as a veteran of this game, I suggest you hold back and wait, it's not worth the hard drive space as of this moment.
