Xenonauts is a strategy game where you command the titular international military group tasked with defending Earth from alien invasion in the late 1970s. It's supposed to be a remake of the original X-Com set during the Cold War, and it's a pretty faithful recreation right down to the battlefield, base placement and troop equipment micromanagement. The inclusion of real-world weaponry in particular gives it a hard sci-fi tinge that the newer XCOM games don't have, and it is indeed deeper than the newer XCOM series, not that those newer games are worse for it. However, the lack of any sort of tutorial hurts the game's accessibility for anyone who isn't familiar with classic X-Com.
For me personally, it feels more like a classic Doctor Who serial without the Doctor or indeed almost any sense of optimism. (It doesn't really take advantage the fact that it's set during the Cold War; often you'll have NATO and Warsaw Pact soldiers working together in the same squad.) This game can be pretty brutal at times. The only thing that will save you from the nasty, aggressive aliens is attacking them wherever it's advantageous to do so - determing when that is being a whole other conundrum - with maximum firepower, then stealing their stuff so your scientists can reverse-engineer it into even
firepower.
Air combat is perhaps the best expansion over the original X-Com, though it's 3v3 max, horizontal only and takes some getting used to. Knowing the limits of your aircraft at any given time and putting some thought into how you launch them against alien ships is crucial, given how crucial the air war is to begin with. In other words, thoughtlessly deploying will get your planes shot down more often than not.
I quite like the game, and it's an impressive indie effort, so I'd say it's good...but it's a bit rough around the edges. As mentioned before, for instance, there's no real in-game tutorial. You either learn by very very painfully doing, or you seek out community help to understand the game.
Breaching downed alien ships can become tedious - the devs should have added back doors, side entrances and/or destructible hull points to at least some of them. You pretty much need explosives, shields and/or expendable soldiers because at least some of the aliens will have holed up inside and they're usually more than willing to go all Scarface on whoever's unfortunate enough to walk in first.
The original X-Com eventually gave you tools to counter psionic attacks and develop your own. Xenonauts doesn't give you anything of the sort except letting your braver troops/those who survived previous psychic attacks resist them more effectively.
Bullet trajectories aren't modeled past your units' line of sight, from what I can tell. If you fire on where you know an alien is, but the alien is out of your LOS, it won't do anything unless you use projectile weapons such as rockets. Lines of sight themselves can be weird: soldiers seem to have a difficult time throwing grenades over objects, but alien forces seem to be able to see your forces often before you can see them.
Workshop support is truly this game's saving grace. There's already a number of mods that try to improve the game in their own ways, most prominently a Community Edition that's been made semi-official by the game's own developers.
Overall I would say this is a very enjoyable game if you're into the strategy genre and don't mind a challenge. It's certainly smoother around the edges for people who feel the original X-Com is too old, and it's faithful enough for people who
played the original to enjoy as a competent remake.
The prequel novella included with the game is good, too.

Xenonauts is an echo from a time when XCOM was X-Com.
What makes the game good is not that it hails from X-Com, but rather adds a new life to the game, further expanding on what makes X-Com good.
For one, the game's updated graphics allows for the concept of cover to now be a thing, rather than hoping that this wall is going to save me.
Secondly, the game adds in different weapons to help breach those pesky UFO doors and not get mowed down in the process.
Third, the game does not shaft newer players in the first month, rather, it shafts players in a long, drawn-out, painful fashion.
If you want to play X-Com, but don't feel like running DOSbox to play it, or want to see what it'd look like with a updated graphical engine, this game is for you.

This game is a platform mining adventure with Metroidvania elements. One might compare it to Terraria where you can dig the ground for mineral ores, but unlike Terraria, the ores cannot be used to build things, instead they are sold for upgrades used to facilitate the players' trek deep into the mines. As you dig deeper, you'll find dungeons that give you extra powers, or extra ores or both that helps you explore the mines even further. You'll also discover caves, and larger structures as you dig. This emphasis on mining for valuable ores and underground exploration, coupled with the ability to place torches, ladders and explosives, as well as the random generation of mines every time you start a new game puts it closer to Spelunky than anything else. However, unlike Spelunky, you don't have to worry about losing your pick axe or dying too much, since you can simply be reassembled for half your money, and you can easily pick your ores back up again.
This game has a lot of things going for it. Just the setting alone capured my interest. You play as Rusty, a steampunk robot in a Western style setting who had just inherited the mines from his now-deceased uncle. Your task then, is to take up his mantle and explore the mines yourself and find out what he was up to before he bought the farm. The game world features beautiful sprite work and a charmingly cute art style that is very reminiscent of modern 2-D sprite platform games. The gameplay is also pretty cathartic and relaxing with how easy it is to get into and how unstressful it is. The idea of carving your own underground world is also pretty attractive. The porting job done from the 3DS to Steamworks is also pretty nice as it works really nicely with an XBox 360 or simillar controller out of the box and there are no stretching or forced aspect ratio involved. It actually looks very crisp and clean with no artifacts of resizing to be found.
However, there may be some things that could put off potential buyers from picking this game up. For one, the game is really short, lasting 5 hours on average or 7 if you're thorough like me. The combat can be pretty awkward due to the randomly generated nature of the mines placing some enemies in awkward places to fight, and as far as boss fights go, there is just the one toward the end. Some people might also be disappointed by the lack of challenge often associated with a game with Metroidvania elements.
All the same, I would recommend this game to anyone looking for a fun single-player casual mining platformer adventure to pass the time. The randomly-generated nature of the mines means that there is quite a lot of replay value to be had with this game. For just 10 Dollars, you can definitely do much worse than pick this game up.

A timeless classic. It has all the usual features that RTS games of that time tended to have.. and more!
Here are some features that make this game especially awesome and which many contemporaries lack (e.g. AoE, Warcraft, C&C):
- automatic infinite production loops of units (so you don't click yourself to death trying to constantly refill the ranks of your troops)
- armies CAN get huge (easily over 1,000+ per player) and WILL get huge (due to the ease of producing lots of units)
- more realism: your swordfighters won't be able to hit a building with melee weapons magically setting it on fire and eventually destroying it, instead, most buildings can be captured, and buildings can be destroyed only using artillery or certain specific unit types (standard settings)
- very flexible game speed (single player only): you can play it really slow to follow every single move your units make, useful when building up a base, or insanely fast to the point where you'll have trouble keeping up with understanding whats going on during a battle
10/10 best game, best game

After reading the reviews I still wasn't sure whether this game was for me, but I decided to try the demo. Now, having played for several hours and intending to play for several more, I can say with confidence that it is.
Pros:
- The randomized loot leads to a lot of playstyle variety, not only due to the stats but because each kind of weapon feels very different from the others
- It's extremely satisfying to play
- It's fast-paced enough that it doesn't get dull
- Moving around is genuinely fun. It may not be for everyone, but personally I think the double jumping and teleporting feels fluid and fun and gives you a lot of options to dodge and strafe in combat
- The music is great
- It's visually appealing
- There are still frequent updates and the dev is very active!
- Along with that, everything is free once you've bought the game
- Though there isn't anything really in the way of a plot yet, I have no doubt that it will make the game even more engaging
Cons:
- If repetition isn't your thing, this may not be the game for you, as there are not many types of enemies and (currently) when you save and quit, your inventory and stats are saved but the world is not, so while you always have a way to get more experience, your progress in the world itself will be reset every time (though after a certain point there aren't really barriers to getting around, other than your level)
- I have high hopes for the eventual plot, but as it stands right now, let's face it: there isn't one. If plot-based games appeal to you, it may be a safer bet to wait and see what this holds
- While there is multiplayer, it's almost always empty or any servers up are private
- Gold seems incredibly useful at first, but after a short while you will have more than you could ever need and nothing to spend it on (yet?)
- For some reason there is a (seemingly arbitrary) cap on getting perks and talent points - you can only have 3 perks (which have various effects in specific situations), some of which aren't very useful, and you only get talent points (which improve your various abilities) up until you're lvl 50. While there may be a good reason for the limit, it currently just makes me wary about putting talent points into anything in the event that I regret it - they cannot be refunded once you've locked them in, and as said before, they're limited
In terms of the actual gameplay I would liken it somewhat to the Borderlands series - there is an emphasis on swapping your weapons out for better ones regularly, to customize your inventory according to what playstyles you enjoy, and the randomization means you may have to make a few tough decisions based on flat-out damage versus useful side benefits.
Overall, the graphics, gameplay, and music combine to make Black Ice - in my opinion - a game more than worthy of its price and your time. And if you're not convinced, play the demo! It did a fantastic job of displaying the gameplay and convinced me that it was entirely worth paying for.
This game is a perfect time killer, and the visual aspects of the game make you interested in it as well.

I only have 4 hours on this game at the time of writing this review, but I've already decided my verdict. This game is amazing for many different reasons.
1. No Tutorial
-Yes, this may be a bit harsh at first, but it actually lets you get right into the game, no pauses, no stops, no obstacles. The game starts you next to a deposit of Resin, so you can make your base.
2. Difficulty
-This game is NOT an easy or rewarding game in any way. You found some copper ore? Ha! You don't have a smelter! You found some stuff to make a smelter? Oops! You fell into a cave and died! And lost your stuff unless you can get there again. Oh you got your stuff and made the smelter? No electricity to run it! But this makes the game so much more fun, and one must devise interesting strategies to move on.
3. Vehicles
-The first vehicle you can make is the rover, then the truck(you don;t have to make them in order, just that the rover needs copper which is more common), then the shuttle, then the bigger spaceship(name?). The vehicles add an incredible element of quick transportation, although the land vehicles are definitely strange to drive. Every vehicle requires fuel, with the space-faring ones requiring hydrazine, and the land-faring requiring electricity.
4. Terrain Shaper
-This tool adds an extremely interesting element to the game as one can shape the terrain freely(as long as they have power to spare), which makes for exilerating gameplay and spelunking.
5. Other Cool Elements
-Things like hooking rovers to trucks to make a car train, the orbit map, stuff like that.
There are some bad things though...
1. BUGS
-Although they're usually minor, they're everywhere, and some ingenuity is required to circumvent them.
2. Oddities in the Game
-Things like the fact that once you build a shuttle, you can't build any other vehicle without a new vehicle bay, stuff like that.
3. No Timewarp
-After you land on, say the exotic planet, likely your home planet will be out of range, meaning you have to wait about 5 minutes, doing NOTHING. Please add a timewarp function, please.
CONCLUSION:
A very fun game, totally worth the $20 spent. Very challeging, but fun. I highly recommend that you buy this game, especially now, while it's only $20 and likely to vastly improve over its lifetime. Definitely one of the best games I've played in a while.

I would say this is currently the best fighting game on the market. The game shines and excels in pretty much every element. It might not be the easiest fighter, but it's definitely the one worth learning. Anyways, let me explain a bit more in detail what makes this game so damn good.
Characters: Every character in roster feels unique and interesting, be it when it comes to the gameplay itself, their design, or their backgrounds and personalities, which you will see both in story and in gameplay itself. They even have special interactions between each other during combat(while executing certain special moves or instant kills), and things like that really add to the overall experience.
Gameplay: Fighting is fun and fast paced, although it isn't the simplest fighter out there, since it has quite a lot of mechanics that you will probably need to learn if you wanna play well. Still, it doesn't feel overwhelming and it's definitely worth learning. When it comes to characters, no character feels the same and they often have some very character-specific mechanics(Sin's food meter, Johnny's coins etc.) which adds to their overall playstyle variety and gives a lot of interesting matchups.
Graphics: Best looking fighting game out there, no contest. Great looking backgrounds, amazing looking characters and animations. -SIGN- already looked damn amazing, -REVELATOR- looks even better with some graphical updates like dynamic lighting that affects characters and backgrounds.
Music: Guilty Gear always had an amazing soundtrack and this game is no expection. One of the best soundtracks ever made IMO. There are also tons of hard rock and heavy metal references through the whole game, not only in OST, but also in character designs, move names, story etc. etc. which you will probably appreciate if you like that kind of music. You can also unlock most of the BGMs from previous GG games with in-game money.
Story: Revelator has a non-interactive 5 hour story mode, which is essentially a movie, fully voiced and animated. Story is quite fun and enjoyable, although there's a lot of anime bs in second half.
Tutorial: They made a brand new tutorial for this game, which tries to explain basic fighting game mechanics through mini games. Then there is and advanced section with missions that try to explain some more advanced mechanics through practical use in combat and also matchup specific stuff. For some reason, some of the mechanics, like danger time, aren't explained in either of those two modes, although they are mentioned and roughly explained in FAQ which you can open in pause screen. Not sure why would they bother making a brand new tutorial mode and then omit stuff like that, even though those were all included in -SIGN- tutorial mode.
Other content: Besides stuff mentioned above, there is M.O.M. mode, Arcade mode, Versus Mode Training mode, Online mode with ranked matchmaking and player lobbies, where, besides usual fighting and spectating, you can show off your avatars, emotes and also play football(kind of). There's also a fishing minigame and a Figure mode thing. Not sure what that last one is all about, I guess for making artwork or something. There's plenty of stuff that you can purchase with ingame money, like extra BGMs, colors, avatars, emoticons etc.

This is a very honest review, there's likely going to be no jokes in this one. (TL;DR at bottom)
Okay, so, I played APB Reloaded for a whomping 140.2 hours as of this date, and I have to admit, it has changed since late 2013/early 2014.
Okay, serious now. This game is addicting. It's like GTA's long lost cousin that was maybe what you can say a "failed abortion". You get to be an Enforcer or a Criminal. Enforcers are like cops, but are just vigilantes. Criminals are the most un-guessable thing ever. Criminals. That's what they are.
There are many ways to make money as a criminal, which would most commonly be known as ram raiding, or missions or even mugging. (Although it doesn't give you a lot if they don't drop anything.) Now, to make a lot of money as an Enforcer, is to witness someone and take their stuff which starts a mission, or be a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and take their van full of stuff to an Enforcer fence. (I don't know what they're called.)
Controls are simple, you hit F to interact, WASD to move, ~ to put away your weapons, and LMB to shoot, and RMB to aim with Q and E as your lean buttons, all of which can be changed.
Combat is pretty fun. You hit G to throw a grenade, and if you hold it, you can actually survive it somehow.
Vehicles are great, you can either drive, or if you're in a team/group together, you can be a passenger. As a passenger, you can hit A or D to lean out the window and fire at other things (Only with specific weapons.).
Character customization is insanely good. You can change everything about your character. It goes down to the bone. (Literally.)
Overall, (TL;DR) this game is fun. It's even better with friends, and I've already made some while playing this game. The community can be bad, but there's always that small group of people that are willing to have fun blowing up a bunch of cars and smashing into stuff in a garbage truck. A F2P Zombie survival game, currently NOT P2W. It's from Free Reign which is a developer/publisher which has changed their name numerous times (Stellar Stone/Online Warmongers/Hammerpoint Interactive/OP Productions/Arktos Entertainment Group/Free Reign). Mostly known for 'WarZ' later to be known as 'Infestation: Survivor Stories' (ISS) a quick google of Sergey Titov will give the reader untold amounts to read through. I'm personally not privy to any of it, but the end result, bad taste and fallout has not been in Free Reign's favour, with many gamers feeling burnt by it all. Thats as much as I want to talk about (some of ) the (remaining WarZ) team behind Aftermath and with that lets talk about the game. Got to say that it's Romero's Aftermath as in Romero's son (George Cameron Romero) and not George A. Romero.
I for one came late to what was ISS. I enjoyed ISS as my playtime was mainly free of the issues (Hackers) and makers mistakes (Market/Revive) that plagued it earlier. Aftermath plays like ISS at its core, the main focus is PVP gameplay which was ISS main/only pull. I'm glad to report that there is now a stamina limit for the Immersion destroying bunny jumping that was the PVP norm in ISS. There are also PVE servers but these currently act more as a gun loot hunt for filling up the GI for PVP action later.
PVP or PVE servers, its good to know loot spawns are aplenty although, looting for 30 mins can have you overloaded with shotguns (sweepers) and pistols it could do with more ammo drops. Melee in Aftermath is subpar to be truthful, god awful is another way of putting it. Funnel the zombies through a doorway and they will happily wait in line for you to jab them in the face one at a time. Out in the open also easy to out smart. Only Zombie danger I feel is that I've got close enough to its radus for it to burst into action like a homing missile an grope me from behind. Zombies don't wander much either so its possible to judge this 'zombie radus' and loot Scot free (running will increase their radus, so don't run).
Crafting is in Aftermath, I've not spent to much time with it but. You require plans for every item in game, every item can be broken down into craftable items and there is craftable items to be looted all around too. So far I have about 5-6 plans which have been repeating themselves a little too often. Base building also shows it face, likewise not touched much of it, to judge.
The map is large enough in my view with enough points of interest, but more variety is needed, both in town and out. Dessert areas are barren and require at least zombies to populate as zombies are currently only dotted about tents and buildings.
Its good to see that, Free Reign have taken a leaf out of ISS Thailand's book with novice servers as a starting point for new accounts. This sounds 'so what'ish but the effect is a lot less hackers and cheaters on non-starter servers. I'm glad that steps have been put in place other than just anti-cheat. Developers should take cheaters seriously the effects can make or break a IP. In ISS's case drive the playerbase away.

Aftermath is still early in development, nothing special so far. I still feel that if, you enjoyed ISS it should be at least downloaded and given a go. If ISS or the survival thing just doesn't do it for you Aftermath will not change your mind. Aftermath will not given sleepless nights to DayZ, 7DTD, H1Z1, Rust or many other more polished titles but these are all paid titles and Aftermath is free.

If the genre interests you, definitely give this one a shot- it might be exactly what you're looking for. The crafting/building system is fun and PVE is an enjoyable environment to play in. Plenty of opportunities for those groups and individuals that like to create their own narrative or roleplay.

It could use a good wiki, though. There's a lot of depth to crafting/health/hydration that is challenging to pick up on the fly.
Not a fanboy, but this one deserves a chance.
As an aside, the zombie ai works for me and its what i've been a fan of since seeing the original DotD in the 70s. (slow and stupid, but don't get caught in a pack or get too ambitious.)

SteamWorld Dig is an interesting game, but with a number of missed opportunities.
The look and feel of the game is really great, especially the artwork. Gameplay consists of (1) digging (2) acquiring ore (3) selling ore (4) beating set levels. The main maps are randomly generated, but the set levels are fixed. I really enjoyed the set levels, and appreciated the care put into the puzzles. Though not particularly difficult, they were interesting. The randomly generated maps are frustrating after a time. The biggest missed opportunity in this game is to do more with the very brief set levels. The other missed opportunity is that it doesn't make much difference which ores you are digging, the only distinguishing feature is how high a price they fetch from the vendor. When you're mining, there's no obvious way of telling which ore you're digging up, which does matter for bagspace, especially if you find a valuable gem. It also feels like there might have been more benefit from being able to craft some items from certain ores.
The end of the game was surprisingly frustrating, and I felt a bit annoyed at being forced to backtrack through the levels.
In all, it was fun, and worth it for the sale price. I hope that there will be a sequel with some added improvements.

I like platformers. I especially love Spelunky and Super Meat Boy. I also enjoy games like Guacamelee and Raymond. So if you like them too you'll probably not like this game. I also like sandbox games like terraria and starbound. So this review might be helpful for people with the same taste. Don't expect from this game too much. It'll take 2-3 evenings. But before I count things I don't like I'd prefer to show positive side of deal:
+ there is a plot
+ funny NPC characters, their phrases
+ beautiful simple picture
That's all. It's ok for $4 game (I bought it during sale), but anyway I regret that I spent time and money for it. Now check things I don't like about this game:
- It's really short. It took less than 5 hours to pass it completely including all "puzzle" caves. According to the game plot It has a claim to be continued, but it will be another game or DLC. It's better to be free patch/DLC. Otherwise, it'll not be worth.
- Simple. No challenges at all. It's like walking in the park. Game process is slow and smooth. I didn't feel my self in dangerous until I met a boss. There is only one boss at the end of the game. Regular monsters are dump and predictable. They are easy to avoid or kill. Few "puzzle" caves require 2-5 minutes to pass because of they are obvious. And it's not big deal to die as you will be resurrected.
- Routine. Yep, it's all about digging. Get deeper to get more resources to sell it to get more money to upgrade your ammunition to be able to get deeper... you got it. Defeat final boss.
- Replayability. There is no replayability. No score table to compare your and another players progress, crack a records. No difficult levels.
- More fun with company? No, thank you. I've got used to play with my wife together or with friend of mine. Games like Spelunky, Guacamelee allow me to enjoy company and a game at the same time. Regarding to SteamWorld Dig there is no multiplayer or hot seat. It's obvious from the game description but it's pity anyway.
It's not an ideal game or a masterpiece. Just be ready if you're going to play. On the other hand, it was disposable fun you can enjoy yourself anyway and may be like it. Frankly, I can't recommend this game. I hope my review was helpful for you.

This game released on Early Access three years ago and still receives major content updates.
10/10 would experience Early Access as Valve intended again.

What can I say? This is a surprisingly polished game, despite being in "early access." It has a demo (which seems to be a rather uncommon feature lately), it is visually appealing, and it has one of the nicest developers I've seen in a while. As far as gameplay goes, this game is perfect for a relaxing time mowing down enemies, while never even approaching boring you. Somehow, it accomplishes relaxed excitement, at least the way I play it. With a great soundtrack that complements the action, this game feels quite complete, and yet keeps expanding with new additions. Although my hours don't quite reflect it, I really do enjoy every bit of playing this game.

Before you continue, try the Demo. After that, add this game to your "Following" list. The developer has got a good thing going here, and I hope the game and its following continues to grow. But as of now I cannot recommend buying this game.
So let's get straight to the point. The biggest, scariest, most crippling flaw of this game is the limited content. The gameplay is beyond repetitive, the world gets old fast, and the game lacks any sort of direction or motivation. Remember the demo, you played it up to level 4? Unfortunately, the paid game is the exact same as the demo. There is no plot, the enemies stay the same, the weapons hardly change, it's literally just like playing the demo over and over again for hours on end. At the time of typing this I've logged about 5 hours, and the game has been pretty much the same for every moment of it. There IS some sort of "final boss", Finality Inc, but there's really no motivation to shoot for it and complete the game when the final boss is really just a higher-level version of the tutorial server.
This should be fine, though. The game IS in early access. It's not supposed to be complete. But what concerns me is how close it appears to be to completion. The game is in beta 8.0, meaning the game may have only two more major updates until the full release. The developer has also stated that he will slowly increase the price of the game as it continues development until the game launches at a final price of $20, and the game is already sitting at $15. I feel this game should be sitting firmly in the pre-alpha state, not an update or two from launch. I'd love to see this game grow, but I fear the game will cut development short before it can achieve its real potential. As a result, I sadly can't recommend early access fans invest in it.
If you feel like supporting a nice indie game company and have some cash to blow, go right on ahead. But for most people I think this game is not worth the investment. That said, follow the game's development and cross your fingers.

I only have 4 hours on this game at the time of writing this review, but I've already decided my verdict. This game is amazing for many different reasons.
1. No Tutorial
-Yes, this may be a bit harsh at first, but it actually lets you get right into the game, no pauses, no stops, no obstacles. The game starts you next to a deposit of Resin, so you can make your base.
2. Difficulty
-This game is NOT an easy or rewarding game in any way. You found some copper ore? Ha! You don't have a smelter! You found some stuff to make a smelter? Oops! You fell into a cave and died! And lost your stuff unless you can get there again. Oh you got your stuff and made the smelter? No electricity to run it! But this makes the game so much more fun, and one must devise interesting strategies to move on.
3. Vehicles
-The first vehicle you can make is the rover, then the truck(you don;t have to make them in order, just that the rover needs copper which is more common), then the shuttle, then the bigger spaceship(name?). The vehicles add an incredible element of quick transportation, although the land vehicles are definitely strange to drive. Every vehicle requires fuel, with the space-faring ones requiring hydrazine, and the land-faring requiring electricity.
4. Terrain Shaper
-This tool adds an extremely interesting element to the game as one can shape the terrain freely(as long as they have power to spare), which makes for exilerating gameplay and spelunking.
5. Other Cool Elements
-Things like hooking rovers to trucks to make a car train, the orbit map, stuff like that.
There are some bad things though...
1. BUGS
-Although they're usually minor, they're everywhere, and some ingenuity is required to circumvent them.
2. Oddities in the Game
-Things like the fact that once you build a shuttle, you can't build any other vehicle without a new vehicle bay, stuff like that.
3. No Timewarp
-After you land on, say the exotic planet, likely your home planet will be out of range, meaning you have to wait about 5 minutes, doing NOTHING. Please add a timewarp function, please.
CONCLUSION:
A very fun game, totally worth the $20 spent. Very challeging, but fun. I highly recommend that you buy this game, especially now, while it's only $20 and likely to vastly improve over its lifetime. Definitely one of the best games I've played in a while.

In all honesty, I was concerned about the PC port on the basis of how atrocious the Dark Souls port was. After doing some research from reviewers that got their hands on the game early along with PC gameplay trailers being released, the more confident I became in From Software creating a stable port. As a result, the PC port plays much better than it's console counterparts running at full 60 FPS with no fluctuations and being more optimized for mid build PC's and higher end with full graphics customization that Dark Souls originally lacked. Overall it is a phenomenal port and it is clear that From Software put in the time and dedication to making Dark Souls II accessible on PC and an extremely enjoyable experience. I have been a fan of the Soul's Series since the start of Demon Souls and I highly recommend this game.

To those of you who have never played dark souls or have been living under a rock, The souls games are challenging-yet-rewarding Role Playing Games. Dark Souls 2, is of course, no different. This game offers about 40-50 hours of content in a single playthrough for the first time, average player. You'll fight bosses, you'll probably get invaded by other players, and you're probably going to die. A lot. Yet despite that, through perseverance you will have some of the most satisfying moments you have ever experienced in a videogame. The game has a brilliant atmosphere, a distinct sense of loneliness despite the game's multiplayer functionality. There's plenty of indepth lore to be discovered if you're willing to look for it, or it can be ignored entirely. That's part of the beauty of the game. There's plenty to do, with new game+ modes, Player Versus Player, and the stat system and variety of weapons Dark Souls 2 offers, and you will definitely need more than one playthrough to see it all. The combat is weighty, yet responsive and feels realistic, especially with improvements made to how  armour weight works in dark souls 2. Dark souls 2 does have its flaws, Sometimes multiplayer connections are not the greatest, the game has a few balancing issues (nothing major), and the Keyboard and Mouse controls on the PC version of the game are less than adequate. You will probably require an xbox controller to play this game.
I will say that having extensively played the PS3 version of the game in the month or so it's been out and having now played the PC version, that the PC version is definitely the platform on which Dark Souls 2 should be played. The experience runs at a smooth 60 frames per second and the textures are much higher resolution than the console version.
I'd personally give the game an 8.5/10. It's a solid title with some flaws, and definitely a lot more challenging than the majority of games that are released in today's market.

LEGO, Batman, computer games...you would think combining them would create something wonderful. Sadly, not with 'LEGO Batman' and 'LEGO Batman 2'. I played 'LEGO Batman' and didn't really like it, thinking it was rather dull, frustrating, and hard to control with the keyboard. I later went on to 'LEGO Batman 2', hoping and half expecting improvements.
'LEGO Batman 2' is a whimsical and charming game, and improved upon its predecessor by having actual voice acting in the game. (The first game just featured characters making sound effects, like grunting.) However, this game still has the clunky keyboard controls (the default configuration makes no sense to me), unfriendly camera angles, and wonky pathfinding from the first.
In the end, 'LEGO Batman 2' is a mediocre PC port of a console game at best. TT Games did not bother to optimize it for the PC. The game does not automatically start in your system's default graphic resolution on the first run, which is unacceptable for a modern PC game. Plus, 'LEGO Batman 2' is best played using a controller because its keyboard controls are unintuitive. Reconfiguring the default keyboard controls improved my gaming experience a bit, but I still had to fight the weird game camera positioning.
Furthermore, 'LEGO Batman 2' is really designed for co-op play because the character that I was not controlling was not helpful in fighting off bad guys and solving puzzles in the single-player mode. Yet, the game does not offer online multiplayer. Having two people playing side-by-side may be nice (and nostalgic) if it is done on a console, but less ideal on a PC, especially if both players have to huddle around a single keyboard. That may be acceptable or tolerable back in the early 90s, but not in the 2000s.
Both 'LEGO Batman' and 'LEGO Batman 2' capitalize on our love of LEGO and Batman. It is unfortunate that TT Games did not put a bit more effort into making 'LEGO Batman 2' more PC-friendly, let alone improving on its gameplay. It is frustrating and disappointing to see TT Games seemingly coast in what they do despite having the lucrative properties of LEGO and DC characters to work off of.

Lego Batman 2 DC Super Heroes is yet another yet another LEGO game made by Travellers Tales. This one released in 2012. Yep, casual platformer, but the first Lego game with talking characters and free-roam. It also came out for Xbox 360, PS3, Wii, WiiU. And it also had handheld versions which are Nintendo DS, 3DS and PS Vita. They are quite different. Like, a lot of stuff in gameplay is different, levels were changed around, abilities. Oh, and no free-roam.
Consoles also had DLC and achievements. No achievements for Steam. As for DLCs, you are missing out on Heroes and Villians packs, each with 5 characters. Which are probably as good as reskins.
Technically, while it's better optimized than Lego Harry Potter 5-7, it's still known to be quite buggy. It still crashes sometimes, you see. I actually had two crashes in a row for pre-last level. Well, at least this game also introduced checkpoint saves.
It also was using the language that I had on my OS/computer, not what I set in Steam. Which annoys me, since hearing voice in English and seeing subtitles in different language confuses my mind, as I understand both. No, translation wasn't word-to-word, that's why.
Anyway, once again, it's a casual 3D platformer where you have infinite lives, has almost no challenge in combat, beat up everything to collect as much studs as possible to unlock neat stuff of tons of chars and collecting everything.
Again.
But this time with new additions.
Again.
If forget that these new additions are quite important to Lego series.
For normal levels there isn't much new to write about. They seem a bit more fun. And whole combo-numbers thing changed: instead of working as studs multiplier like in the first game, it does something else. If you do a throw on enemy while the combo is ongoing, upon death he will drop 100 * Combo Number of studs. And if you do the finishing move thing, the combo number will be doubled. It's not exactly as enganging mechanic, just kinda there to make you vary things up, I guess. Shame that x10 is the max.
Oh, and no more vehicle levels. Instead we have on-rails shooter. Which is nice fun, sensetive aiming aside.
Now, as for important ones, characters can now talk and hub got expanded enough to be counted as free-roam now.
Thanks to characters talking, the plot stepped up. While many will miss lego meme action, I think that it's a welcome feature. Like a good action/adventure/comedy, the story is quite awesome in this one, enganging. It sure beats a bit of repetetiveness of Lego games. It sure shows that this game for once has it's own storyline instead of being forced to do what movies have. Well, if forget that it also flopped a bit: It seems to mostly focus on Batman and Superman vs Lex Luthor and Joker. No villian story. And the other DC heroes, which are Justice League, appear only in the last two short levels. For shame!
Ah well, at least it's awesome to play as overpowered Superman.
Heck, there even was "Lego Batman Movie" released in the next year, which is based on plot of this game, even using modified cutscenes from here.
And then there is freeroam. Between missions and so you can explore the Gotham city, which is three island with tall buildings. And tall buildings. With lots of goodies hidden in them. And you might think: Hey, I can just fly with Superman to get all the goodies. Not to mentioning that game playes Superman theme when you fly with him, which is super awesome. But sadly, the flying control in free-roam sections is badly done. I mean, it's all fine when you are just flying, but when you want to land on top of building then it goes awry. I don't feel like descripting so I shall just yell ARGH. There, good enough of explanation?
Fine. It's mostly because you can't just drop immeditly to the ground and trying to tilt character down to the ground while flying will probably making him suddenly turn around and refuse to land. Or don't know, it's just painful.
Then again, game itself thinks that it would be too easy if you want to get gold bricks this way and instead it will want you to find Robin or Batman costume on the ground and then climb on top of building without losing it by changing character. Which is fun from what I tried so far. Yay climbing.
Navigating through it isn't as easy either. Sure doesn't help that path-studs seems to not always appears in time or take sharp turns.
Anyway, for story walkthrough it was a fun game that I beat on a single breath, but I am not sure how it is when trying to collect everything. Still will take it over older titles.

As far as I can tell, this is probably the most friendly fighting game on the current market for newcomers to fighting games. Aside from having probably the best cell-shaded graphics on the market (where the characters pretty much look like they would in 2-D), and one of the best soundtracks, the game also goes a step further and has a story that...while not the best, is defintely fun enough to watch.
Unlike it's predecessor, -Sign-, -Revelator- Includes the "stylish" fighting style. This is very similar to Marvel Vs Capcom's "Easy" Controls from dreamcast. When you mash certain buttons, you will perform a combo of attacks, and you also are given a special button to do certain overdrive moves. It does have many downsides, as it will make your character weak than Technical, on top of limiting your combos to only what the game gives you. But if you are completely new to fighting games and just want to jump in to the single player and try to enjoy it before you learn, then this is a very good option to do so. I do not recommend it for multiplayer unless you are against someone else using stylish, however.
The story mode has a huge fault due to being non-interactive, however it also has the plus of being an unfragmented, fairly decent 3-4 hour story. And on top of this, you still have the typical Arcade mode and M.O.M. (which is basically a replayable single player mode). To add though, unlike -Sign-, -Revelator- does not have dubbed voices, meaning you will have to read everything you see.
While I have not personally experienced the multiplayer, I have heard that -Revelator- has some of the best balance. As said though, if you wish to play competitively, you will need to gradually switch off of Stylish and learn all the moves and combos to really enjoy it.
Pros: Good Multiplayer, 2 Single Player Modes, Stylish moveset for new players, technical for veteran players, one of best albums in gaming, beautiful looking game, probably the best story as far as fighting games go.
Cons: non-interactive story (a con for some), very high learning curve if not using stylish, competitive stylish is impossible, must read all dialogue to appreciate story
I would recommend this game to hardcore fighters who just want a solid fighting game, but can also recommend it to player's wanting a fighting game they can play single player, especially if they haven't yet learned fighting game mechanics.
If the price goes down, such as a discount, I would even recommend it for the story alone. Though you will also need -Sign- to get the entire story!

Ok, so before I start, let me make one thing unmistakably clear: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO HAVE GODLIKE EXECUTION TO BE GOOD AT THIS GAME. Guilty Gear is a game about spacial awareness, about knowing your opponent, about doing the right thing at the right time. None of these things are Combo Video-level execution. GET THIS INTO YOUR HEAD. I play Pot, okay? I can't do 6K loops to save my life. My motor abilities rival those of a trained orangutan. And yet, I still win matches. It can be done, people.
Alright, with that out of the way: This game is the full package. Deep, nucanced, fast-paced, balanced for fun and yet every character is 100% tournament viable. The amount of mechanical freedom you're given can be overwhelming at first, but once everything clicks, the battlefield becomes a canvas that you paint on. If you like you express yourself through your playstyle, look no further. No two Kys play quite the same, no two Slayers play quite the same. Every Millia plays like an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, but still, you feel the little differences from player to player. I guarantee you.
And Xrd rewards good reads like almost no other fighting game does. Every tool has a clear counter, and every counter can be baited. Hell, you have about five different options from blockstun alone. And nobody expects you to learn all of these from day 1 onwards. But what you have to understand is that playing this game is a learning process pretty much all the way through. There is no shame in burning all your meter on Faultless Defense, just like there are no "optimal" ways to play your Character.  There aren't even real optimal combo routes most of the time. Instead, you will find yourself observing your position on the screen and adjusting your punishes accordingly. If you're coming from Street Fighter V, where frame data is everything, this will absolutely blow your mind at first. But again, when you're finally starting to get it, you will wonder how a sterile, mathematical system like the one in SFV can even be considered "fighting", really.
Finally, this game is absolutely breathtaking, on both a technical and an artistic level. If you even have a passing interest in 3D-modelling, this is the absolute cream of the crop. Character models morph and smear, with multiple shaders giving the game an impression if having animated 2D-Sprites. Occasionally, the game pans around the action to remind you that, no, these are actually 3D models, and they look fan-♥♥♥♥ing-tastic. The same can be said for the soundtrack, with Hard Rock and Metal riffs blasting trhough your speakers. J-Metal might not be everyone's cup of tea and it certainly isn't mine, usually. But Revelator remains one of the few fighting games where I still listen to the soundtrack instead of my own playlist.
I mean, yeah, it's kind of expensive for an impulse buy, I get it. But look at me: I just wrote a 500-word essay on this game. And you read it, apparently (thanks, by the way). Here's the deal: I spent about 200 hours in SFV before I realized I just wasn't enjoying myself like I hoped I would. I am having *fun* in Xrd, more than I ever had in the Street Fighters. That's all I care about. Buy this game, you won't regret it.

I really wanted to like this game. After all, everyone else seemed to. I have A LOT of steam games and have trouble passing up a promising game when it goes on sale. This was the case with SteamWorld Dig. I read the reviews, looked at the screen shots, checked out the forums, etc. and this definitely sounded like a game that I would enjoy. It looks like bastion and looked like it would play like Terraria's awkward little brother. With that said, I was pretty disappointed when I realized that this game is essentially all of the mining components of Terraria without any of the depth of either of the aforementioned games. This game is great for killing some time, but that's about all it is: a time killer. I didn't laugh at all, and found it to be more or less a grind without any of the payout. It's linear - literally. You have a map that clearly shows that you cannot go right or left anymore, and you just keep digging down. Your pickaxe is your weapon and you can upgrade it, but there's no reward for exploration beyond getting a few more orbs or precious stones that you don't really need in the end.
All in all, I beat this game because I paid for it. Had it been a mobile app I would have been a lot less critical, but it's not. I bought it because people were comparing it to games that I love (Terraria, Starbound, Bastion, etc) that are all surprisingly well polished (Starbound is still in the works, but a lot of fun to play) and much deeper than SteamWorld Dig can possibly hope to get. It's a very two dimensional game with a very two dimensional storyline. I kept hoping that it would get better and gain a bit more depth, but that only led to disappointment. I honestly can't recommend this game enough. It distills the idea of a looter shooter down into it's most pure form. It has looting and it has shooting.
More than that, the game embraces it's unusual and interesting art style. Thanks to it's more simplistic and low poly style it's very apparant what is happening on screen. It's rare to feel cheated, after every death you can point back to what went wrong.
It's not a perfect game, but it is an incredibly solid experience that you should try. There are regular updates taking place that are helping to hammer out any kinks and improve the game. Grab a friend or two and go wild.
If you have any complaints, head on over the the Black Ice discord. Garret is one of the most active devs I have ever seen when it comes to community interaction. You can seriously tell how much he cares.

Black Ice is a loot-based fps with an open world that looks somewhat like Tron. Hack into buildings or 'corporations' to level up while defending yourself against swarms of their security measures (creepy digital-insects!) You can swap your sprint and jump modules for better ones if you find them, and if you can't afford a cool-looking high-dps primary lazer, you can just hack into a shop for all of its loot - but be warned, shops have 'security measures' too!

Astroneer is an open world adventure with no actual goal or purpose, but to survive and (eventually) thrive on an exotic and sometimes beautiful world. You have one "ship", (in which you refill your air from when you run out) and you have a vacuum-like tool that sucks up substances (like rocks and soil) and can store them for later use. This vacuum can also place down the sucked substances, for house building, artificial land bridges (as seen on the trailer), and to fix gaps in your planets ground. So why do I give this game a red, glowing thumbs down? Well, the idea of a free roam space adventure is not unique, and Astroneer's execuation was even more boring. There is no purpose in playing the game; no end goal. No achievements in which you can work forward to, and limited crafting and building options that even somehow manage to ruin the pointless survival aspect of the game. Multiplayer is bascially the same game but with up to 4 players. This definetly adds something to the game, since even the worst of games are fun with friends. Overall connection quality of the servers is actaully tolerable.
You may be reading this review, and are still unconvinced on buying this game. You may look at the pictures, trailers, and the multiple Youtube playthroughs, and see opportunity, fun, exploration, and unique sounds and art. And, to a certain extent, the art style and the music are quite good, and the pictures do look visually pleasing, but thats all there is. The idea of the game is unoriginal, if not nonexistant, and the creativity is therefore limited by the idea. That is why I do not like this game, even if the game did come out of Early Access with an enormous amount of updates that fix the bugs and lack of content.
Its very relaxing and has a beautiful world. Also the game runs nice for the graphics. Play with friends for an even better experience.
Expect crashes. Other than that its great. One of the best and most fun early access games I have ever played.

San Andreas for me is the greatest GTA game to ever exist, yes it's an old game, yes the graphics are dated, yes the physics are pretty bad like the lack of Ragdolls, but the game is more then just a game, it's a whole experience that needs to be played by any GTA fan.
Some of the best characters in the whole franchise are in this game, from the Meme King Big Smoke, to Ryder, to Sweet, to Officer Tenpenny, to Madd Dogg and easily to my favourite GTA and one of my favoruite gaming protagonists, mother♥♥♥♥ing Carl Johnson.
Seriously this game is full of memorable characters, even the most minor ones like Carl's girlfriends will stick into your head due to their memorable lines, and for... other reasons involving coffee.
Introduced some of the best mechanics in the whole franchise, which some were sadly lost in GTA IV, but returned in GTA V, these include Modding Cars, Haircuts, detailed character customization and eating food to regain health.
However exclusive to San Andreas is Carl's Muscle and Fat meters which make him change appearence depending on which one is the highest, and it even includes some exclusve voicelines! Seriously play as Fat CJ and try not to laugh, it's impossible!
There is also weapon skills which improve how you perform with certain weapons, the biggest ones is with some SMGs, the normal pistol and the Sawn-off Shotgun, where if you increase their levels enough, YOU CAN DUAL-WIELD THEM! HOW COOL IS THAT? It makes you feel like a total badass and you become so much more powerful.
A fantastic story which I won't spoil, the reasoning of CJ returning to San Andreas abroad is really sad and you want to help him succeed.
One of the best cities in gaming, it squishes Vice City when it comes to detail, it crunchs Liberty City when it comes to sheer size, and it even beats HD Los Santos in GTA V due to having more things to do inside the city, I mean yea HD Los Santos is bigger, but the varation of land scapes is very lacking since there's only pretty much Beach, city and then desert for 90% of the map, while San Andreas includes all 3 of them, but also has forests, mountain ranges, casino areas and just much much more, hell you can even learn whole new fighting styles like Karate!
Honestly this map has been fantastic to play on since day 1 and I can still play on it for years to come.
Like I said the steam version isn't the same as a retail one, so use a downgrader to use mods.
Speaking of the steam version, it's locked at 25 FPS, exceeding that will brake the game sadly, however the older versions didn't have this issue.
Also some songs have been removed due to expired contracts, however they remain in the older versions.
Some missions can cause newer players trouble, like the infamous Train mission and RC missions... which I had no issue on both myself when I started but hey to each their own.
Best GTA overall, it stands against the test of time with pride and is easily an unforgetable experience that everyone needs to try.
So good infact, San Andreas still gets about 1 Million players to this day.

So let's start with the actual game, because that's what you're all here for right?
First impressions are a HUGE thing, especially when you want to keep players playing and encourage other players to start playing. My first 30 minutes of this game were absolutely horrendous. I spent majority of the time running over the terrible looking map and constantly being annoyed by the same grass/flowers textures that would wave into existence 5m from my character. I managed to find several places to loot, finding small amounts of food and water and a LARGE abundance of items that are obviously meant for crafting. Here's the downside to having all those items; before you can properly use most of them, you first need to find blueprints in order to craft even the most basic of items. Want to build a campfire? Gotta find that blueprint first. They don't appear easy to find either- I looted an entire city and did not find a single blueprint of any kind. So 90% of the other items I  found were useless to me.
Sprinting requires no stamina, yet jumping takes it away which ultimately makes no sense. Both sprinting and jumping should decrease stamina. The zombies are a joke, with them doing so very little in the world. I stood 3m away from one without it aggroing and when it finally did aggro, it stutter-stepped everywhere and quickly de-aggroed when I started running away.
The lack of wildlife in a map that houses the perfect environment to house even birds, is quite annoying, given that animals would still be present at the time of this game.
The game itself offers no instructions in regards to things like group-making, crafting and a myriad of other important tasks. I had to do a manual search on the forums to find out how to group with someone, which turns out that you have to enter in a "/" command into chat in order to do so- a very annoying task.
Overall, I wouldn't recommend this game to anyone but if you're looking to at least try it out, go for it. It's free to play, but that doesn't mean it is exempt from being so horrible.
NOW, onto the background of the game and those behind it.
For those of you who don't know, Sergey Titov is a lying and scamming whackjob (just two of the many names he is known by). Before WarZ (Aftermath's predecessor), Sergey was known for his absolutely horrendous game called Big Rigs. This game is broken beyond compare and really tells you just how bad Sergey is at actually making games himself. However, it certainly isn't his worse trait.
In 2012 when the DayZ mod was so popular that those behind it decided to make a standalone game (thus properly beginning the zombie survival mmo genre), Sergey and an associate of his, "RussianKaliber" essentially hijacked the DayZ mod forums and put forth an idea for thier own zombie apolcapyse game. This got people interested and so began the days of WarZ.
During its Alpha stage, WarZ looked to be a promising title, with the developers promising a large amount of very tasty features that would (in theory) make WarZ the amazing zombie game everyone had always wanted. HammerPoint Interactive (the original development team for WarZ) were selling the game on their website for as much as $60 for a Legendary package, which consisted of a large sum of GC, a Legendary user icon both in-game and on the forums and lastly, 6-months of free stronghold server hosting. There were a few other packages available for less cost but the Legendary was the most expensive. Users were told that the game would never be so cheap. We were in for the biggest surprise of the gaming century.
Come official launch day on Steam (Dec 2012), majority of the playerbase were shown just how much of a scam this all was. The game was being sold for a mere $15, it had one map that was only 30% complete (if that), the vast majority of promised features weren't even present in the game, including the promised stronghold servers and the game itself was filled with more bugs than a roach nest. The developers were quiet for days, having taken a small vacation given it was Christmas time and there was no one around to fix their broken game. It was so bad that Valve stepped in and pulled it from Steam and offered refunds to all for the first time ever.
About a week or so later, WarZ was allowed back on Steam, having amended the description on the store page to more accurately reflect the state of the game. The damage was already done though. To make matters even worse, Sergey issued a supposed "apology" letter which actually more blamed the customers for "misreading" the store page than apologising for the ginormous ♥♥♥♥-up he had intentionally made.
From there, matters continued to get worse and worse for not only the paying customer, but also for the company and those inside it. I won't go into full detail of the events that happened in the year 2013 in regards to WarZ, so I'll do a point summary:

For anyone who may or may not understand WHY a forested map would give you less FPS, let me explain it to you. Every tree is considered an object within the game, given that players can collide with them. Now not only can a player collide with trees, but lighting does as well, which results in the engine having to determine shadows and lighting collisions for EVERY tree placed within the world.

This is the 2nd Lego game I've played, the first being Marvel Super Heroes, and I found this game to be quite enjoyable. I enjoyed this a bit more than the Marvel game but I think a lot of that is because I knew what to expect from it and didn't have as much trouble navigating and using the map to find collectibles. The story portion of the game is short but is pretty fun and light hearted, yet fits in well with the DC and more specifically Batman universe. There are a good number of heroes and villains that you can unlock and play as from both the Batman, Superman and Justice League comics for those familiar with the 2 comics. The only downside to this is that there is not a whole lot reason to use more than a handful of core characters that have abilities that you will find useful quite often. But on the other hand, some characters are basically clones of others in terms of their abilities so you can take your pick of who you'd rather play as.
If you want to just play the story mode, you could probably beat it in 10 hours or less. However there is so much more to do between collectibles and replaying levels in Free Play mode to try and find things that you weren't able to when you played in story mode. Also this is a fun game if you have a kid and want to play local 2 player co-op. I've played this some with my nephew who is 5 and while he's still learning, he can actually do pretty well. I would probably say that it's best suited for kids 7+ but still fun to have something that the 2 of you can play. Overall there is a lot to do and if you plan to get 100% as I did, then be prepared to put in some hours. This seems to be a staple of the Lego games based on the 2 I've played. However, my time played as recorded by Steam is a bit exaggerated due to times when I left the game on pause for long periods of time and times that I played with my nephew on a separate file. However, if you want to go for it all, I'd expect 25-30 hours. The only bad thing about the game is that you can only save your progress at checkpoints during levels and usually when you get collectibles it auto-saves. That's why I had to leave the game on pause for long periods of time a few times because I really had to be somewhere and just didn't have time to get to the next collectible or checkpoint. So just keep that in mind when deciding whether or not to continue playing a level, go for particular collectibles, etc.
Overall, I would definitely recommend this game as something fun for all ages of gamers.

If there was a game you could tell that the developer game a damn about, it would be this one. I bought this late 2014 and have seen it go through so many changes via patches and bug fixes. I even talked to the developer once to give my thoughts. Now, playing it again, I can see it has come far.
Black ice is an FPS set in a cyber world where you hack buildings which spawn enemies when hacked. Loot is dropped randomly, ranging from common to epic and unique loot. These can range from mods you equip to gain passive stats, to weapons, to spawning your own minions, to constant heals/reusable instant heals, and actions like jumping, teleporting, and sprinting. Additionally, there is a level and perk system each time one levels up, with the latter gaining one point every ten levels. You can upgrade the former with additions to HP, RAM (think MP that regenerates), ATK and other attributes.
The enemies have intelligent A.I.: melees will attempt to flank you while ranged will shoot and run.
While playing, I found great enjoyment out of grinding for equipment that fit my playstyle and gave excellent passive strats. The game also has multiplayer.
Buying early access games can be a mistake depending on the game; however, this is not one of those mistakes. The game is constantly evolving and bettering itself and I've had a wonderful time playing and getting iced time to time.

The graphics are just so fitting and so is the music. Really pulls you in and overall is so much fun to play. Highly recommend it!

Gold that's hiding behind the hill, my favorite game of this genre. This old school RTS game is based on events which took place during the 17th and 18th centuries in Europe. It offers 16 playable nations and each has its own architectural style, military advantages, technologies and unique units. The 9 campaigns (requires a DLC) and 100 single missions in this game are tough and it makes the game very challenging and therefore I highly recommend it to any classic RTS fan. In my opinion the first three Cossacks games (Cossacks Anthology series) are far better than Cossacks 2. The second game has different mechanics and just isn't as simple and identical to the first game.
EDIT: I forgot to mention that the Steam version of this game
work with the Game Ranger servers or Hamachi at all. This includes LAN as well. If you want to play against other players you will have to own the non Steam version. Luckily I have the orignal CD somewhere laying around, but I find this quite a letdown, but other than that this game is truly outstanding and absolutely worth buying, but I just don't recommend the Steam version (unless you're fine with single player mode).

To those of you who have never played dark souls or have been living under a rock, The souls games are challenging-yet-rewarding Role Playing Games. Dark Souls 2, is of course, no different. This game offers about 40-50 hours of content in a single playthrough for the first time, average player. You'll fight bosses, you'll probably get invaded by other players, and you're probably going to die. A lot. Yet despite that, through perseverance you will have some of the most satisfying moments you have ever experienced in a videogame. The game has a brilliant atmosphere, a distinct sense of loneliness despite the game's multiplayer functionality. There's plenty of indepth lore to be discovered if you're willing to look for it, or it can be ignored entirely. That's part of the beauty of the game. There's plenty to do, with new game+ modes, Player Versus Player, and the stat system and variety of weapons Dark Souls 2 offers, and you will definitely need more than one playthrough to see it all. The combat is weighty, yet responsive and feels realistic, especially with improvements made to how  armour weight works in dark souls 2. Dark souls 2 does have its flaws, Sometimes multiplayer connections are not the greatest, the game has a few balancing issues (nothing major), and the Keyboard and Mouse controls on the PC version of the game are less than adequate. You will probably require an xbox controller to play this game.
I will say that having extensively played the PS3 version of the game in the month or so it's been out and having now played the PC version, that the PC version is definitely the platform on which Dark Souls 2 should be played. The experience runs at a smooth 60 frames per second and the textures are much higher resolution than the console version.
I'd personally give the game an 8.5/10. It's a solid title with some flaws, and definitely a lot more challenging than the majority of games that are released in today's market.

Edit: You can totally go into third-person. Doesn't change the very limited mechanics, but hey, take what you can get, I guess.
So, firstly, I think this should've been a first or third person shooter. A wave and class based shooter with strong team elements would have been way more interesting than yet another bird's eye twin stick.
To elaborate, there is a class with a jetpack. Because of the viewpoint, it's completely useless unless you're facing a boss that can actually catch up to you.
Speaking of bosses, most of them straight up cannot hit you. If you backpedal, they catch up to you, but the wind up takes too long, so you're completely safe. The only actual threats are normal enemies that don't suffer from this problem, and when bosses go for the harvester in a certain gamemode.
As far as I know, all classes have a regeneration gun that has no cooldown or charge. At any time, you can just whip it out, heal completely, heal the harvester, and lose nothing.
Adding to this problem, the AI will sometimes just run away or go for the harvester alone, completely ignoring you. This isn't a problem, unless it's a boss that takes a ton of damage while it hits the harvester for a ton of damage. So, either you lose everything in one shot, or absolutely nothing mattered.
Music is either fine or terrible. It's either Linkin Park/Doom or Mirror's Edge. How it's implemented is also terrible. At the end of a round, the music just cuts to the Mirror's Edge track. It's jarring going from edgy butt-rock to soft pianos with a sudden cut in the middle.
In general, it's pretty boring. You get attacked by dinosaurs, but it's just some creature with no interesting combat elements. There are also humanoids who have guns, and they have mechs that have blade things, but neither of those shake anything up.
TL:DR Should've been a different perspective, very dull, bad enemy movesets, dumb AI, unbalanced both ways seemingly at random, music isn't great.

and mostly i would really not recommend you playing online (as long as you are not confident in your skill in millisecond thinking) since the players mostly consist of veteran players who will beat the hell out of you and probably bore you very quickly. The match making just takes a look on the character level and not an actual player level (it depends on that "one specific character" he played and does not state the general status of the player. so they can simply pick another character they didn't play that much and brutally slay beginners).
but as i said it takes time to get used to the controls and all the "fighting game knowledge" it's just the multi-player which should give the beginners fair chance to learn about this game just bites the dust.
oh, and yeah the story mode is not actual gameplay but you just sit there and watch an 4 hours and half long anime movie which is quite entertaining when you want to watch some anime.
Still good game has got nice waifus and keeps entertaining you as long as you stay away from that multiplayer mode
Verdict:
If you are confident in your skill and familiar with the Guilty Gear Series (OR just want to get some time killing game including an anime movie of 4 hours and half playtime) then a BIG YES
Else if you are looking for a good fighting game to play online then rather NO (except you really don't care about that)

Rev 2 Update:
The Rev 2 update will be coming soon as a $20 DLC update, and if Rev 2 is your first outing to the Guilty Gear series, it'll cost somewhere between $40-50.  I'll post more on that later when it comes out June 1st, but Rev 2 will have a LOT of new features.
The training mode, stylish mode (easier control scheme for beginners) and FAQs are still there, so the game will still help newcomers to the series git gud, but not only that, there will be beginner restricted lobbies that'll keep higher leveled players out so beginners and casual players can enjoy playing the game in relative peace.
Other new lobby features include network colors (up or down arrows of various colors to indicate the level of a player's skill in relation to yours), three win cabinets (where players can go best of three matches in the center of the lobby), and treasure chests (which give you random prizes from the gallery, much like fishing, except they can only be opened once daily).
Seriously, every time Guilty Gear Xrd releases a new update, there's more and more reasons to play it.
Source:
Original Review:
Guilty Gear Xrd -REVELATOR- improves on everything -SIGN- brought to the table,  Blitz shields can now be held for a (blockable) stagger attack, which can even be used in some combos.  The game's still pretty high execution, but some chraacters are easier to play than others.  I'm a Chipp main, so the struggle to git gud is real.  Still, I love how much this game pushes its players.  But don't worry if you're new to fighting games, the tutorial's got you covered, mission mode teaches game mechanics and tips the tutorial doesn't, and combo mode teaches you character specific moves and combos.
Online is more populated than -SIGN- was on Steam because now it's up to date with the console release (until Rev 2 comes out, anyway), and there's people of all skill levels playing at any given time.  There are a lot of people who are REALLY good at the game who you'll probably run into, but there are some beginners as well.
But if you bought the game, and the tutorials, missions and combo modes aren't enough enough to teach you everything you want to know (and they do kinda leave out a few things), check out the Guilty Gear Crash Course on YouTube, dustloop forums or the Guilty Gear Discord channel.  I'll post those at the end of my review in a resources section.
Pros:
The game's cast is extremely diverse, every character has a different fighting style.
The in-game track selection now includes songs from the vocal collection (as well as vocal versions of songs from previous games in the franchise).
Fishing lets you obtain random unlockables pretty cheap, but you'll get a lot of fish (but every 10 fish you get gives you a new unlockable!).
The game gives you so many options at all times.  Once you get a feel for what you can do, situationally, you'll find yourself improving dramatically.  The more time and effort you put into the game, the more it gives back.
If you get exhausted from mission, combo or online modes, play the story mode (recommended if you completed -SIGN-'s story mode (the order of events go -SIGN- arcade mode, -SIGN- story mode, -REVELATOR- episode mode (basically just arcade mode again) and -REVELATOR- story mode.  I really CAN'T stress how good the game's story is.  I have friends who haven't watched it yet and I'm all like "DO IT!"  Seriously, it's so good.
Cons:
The execution barrier and skill of high level players can be intimidating to new players who hop online and suddenly get bodied, BUT DON'T GIVE UP!  And remember to have fun.
They did nerf reversal timing from -SIGN-, so if you really want to do a reversal, you have to wait longer.  But it's better to just block on your wakeup.  Reversals are that bad now.

Now THIS is how you mix different game types together. Steamworld Dig blends together Metroid, Spelunky, and Terraria flawlessly. You play as Rusty, a robot that receives a mine from his uncle. I only have a couple negatives for Steamworld. The music for me was somewhat forgettable, but that's a small complaint for a game of this quality. SteamWorld Dig is an enjoyable exploration game with bright visuals and fun playability. You control Rusty, a little robot that's come to take over his Uncle's Mine. It starts off innocently enough as you mine for gems to make some money, but the deeper you get, weirder things start showing up. The controls are great; I played with an XBox controller so I can't vouch for keyboard. The gameplay ranges from exploration to a bit of action, to a fair amount of platforming. Throughout the game you buy upgrades that allow you to do a lot more, giving the game a Metroid or Castlevania-esque feel at times.
SteamWorld Dig isn't the longest game; there's an achievement for beating it in under two hours. (Though I imagine that's a hard cheevo to get.) My playthrough took five, but I was hellbent on digging up as much gold as I could. It's very enjoyable for what it is, and I could see myself returning to it again for another playthrough.

Before I start this long review, lets just say this isnt a "Is it good or is it bad" review, its more looking at if the game is worth what it has to offer and a few other things. Lets get started!
Lets first look at what this game has to offer. This game is in pre-alpha 0.2.4b. Now, you would be saying "Thats good for a game!" for this, it isnt. A couple weeks ago, the developers said they would release another update soon. They didn't. So far, the game only has 2 areas, one requiring a "Slime Key" to get into. So far, the game offers 4 beginning slimes when you first boot up a new save. Pink Slimes, Tabby Slimes, Rock Slimes, and Phosphor Slimes (not including Tarr). You can get the slime key within the first day, and become OP in around 5-6 hours. Time wise, not enough.
Now, the later game sllimes, there's not too many "Later game" ones. There's the Boom, Honey, and Puddle slimes. Thats about it until they update the game to feature new things.
Slimes, I will try and list them all, but its complicated. Here we go:
-Pink Slime

-Phosphor Slime
-Phosphor Tabby Largo
-Phosphor Boom Largo

-Pink Phosphor Largo

-Honey Phosphor Largo
-Honey Tabby Largo
-Honey Boom Largo
-Pink Honey Largo
-Pink Boom Largo
-Pink Tabby Largo
-Boom Tabby Largo
-Rock Tabby Largo
-Pink Rock Largo
-Boom Rock Largo
Alright, thats all I could find. Its alot of slimes for its early version, but when the FULL release comnes out, the dev team expects a crap ton more than 9 Slimes. TL;DR  Very repetitive.  Hopefully it will improve.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
This game's music is pretty fun, and it's interesting to play for the first twenty minutes.  That's where the value stopped for me.
- There are a lot of different combinations of stats, weapons, buffs, summons, and powerups, but the variation isn't very meaningful.  Gameplay doesn't really change very much, even with abilities and gear that sound drastically different.  It's all ust circle strafe and button mash.
- All weapons, primary and secondary, feel limp and lifeless.
- Some sound effects and ambient noises are pretty loud and ugly, and not in a way that adds to the game.  They're just jarring.
- The infinite, procedurally generated world isn't very interesting, because it's all small variations on a few building types and nearly flat terrain.  What you see in the first few minutes is most of what you'll ever see.
- The world didn't persist for me across sessions.  I kept all my gear, but all the servers I hacked and paths I carved were just gone.  Disappointing.  I hope this is a bug instead of designed into the game.
- Most of the graphics options (EX: screen shake, wireframe mode, etc) are interesting for 5 seconds, but actually hinder gameplay.  Even with the default graphics it's very difficult sometimes to identify enemies or tell friend from foe.
But the biggest problem with this game is that there just isn't that much to do:
1. Go to building.
2. Press button.
3. Circle strafe to kill things.
4. Collect loot.
5. Optionally buy/sell if that loot wasn't good enough.
6. Rinse and repeat.
There isn't any obvious synergy or emergence between different choices, it's just about making your stats bigger and following the 6 steps above.  Despite being infinite, you've seen it all in one short session.  I really wanted to like this game, but I don't.  Sorry devs.  I know this is early access, so I hope this game matures into a more rewarding experience .
